# LLP 3000.000.000.001: Staging with real users

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Implemented
**Systems:** Snapback 4 deployment, password identity, development doors, proof kit
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever (STAGE)
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Revised:** 2026-10-22 (DX6 §11); 2026-10-21 (DX5 §10); 2026-10-19 (DX4 §§8–9); 2026-10-18
**Related:** [Release activation](./3000.000.000-retained-storage-and-hot-release.rfc.md), [Proof kit](./3000.011.003.000.000-packaged-proof-kit.rfc.md), [Store ownership](./3000.019-what-the-builder-still-wrote.rfc.md#34-p8-residency-you-can-see-and-a-cli-that-does-not-fight-the-dev-server)

## 1. Commission and boundary

Implementer: STAGE, 2026-10-18, commissioned by Charlie's wave-16 bakeoff
fixes #1/#4. Ten Muse probes used dev because password-role provisioning
had no single recipe. This amendment supplies that recipe using the existing
signup and service-seat authority. No system seed door is added to serve.
SEC owns self-promotion lints and security invariants; KIT4 owns unrelated
proof helpers, PROD2 owns production starter adaptation.

`deploy <dir> --staging` classifies a **new deployment store**, under its
exclusive owner, with durable metadata `deployment_environment=staging`.
An existing store with no classification is production, including legacy stores;
it cannot be relabelled. A staging store remains staging through deploy,
rollback, restart, copying and source edits. There is no promote/relabel flag:
production requires a separate fresh deployment without --staging and real
operator provisioning. --check never creates the classification. Repeating
--staging on an already staging store is allowed, including while serve runs;
it verifies the existing classification without changing it. Malicious edits by
the filesystem/database owner are outside the threat model, as for service tokens.
This is a deployment-lifetime boundary stronger than a mutable per-release flag:
production source or a seed plan cannot opt a production store into test setup.

## 2. Real staging accounts

`GET /auth/config` reports `development` independently of door availability,
`devDoors`, and `environment` (`development`, `staging`, or `production`).
Missing/unknown environment metadata is production. serve remains bearer-only
in both environments, with the same password verifiers, session lifetimes,
rules, rate limits, clock and data plane. No password hashing or grant bypass.

`startServe(dir, options)` additionally returns `operatorToken(service =
"operator", days = 1)` and `seedAccounts(options)`. Minting uses the existing
local CLI proof protocol, captures secret stdout in memory and never writes
tokens into proof logs. It confers only that service seat's existing authority.
Tokens may also be requested on production for first-admin setup.

`seedAccounts({roles, provision, args?})` creates N real password accounts per
role, then calls the declared mutation as service:operator; `args(account)`
maps the account to application arguments (default `{principal, role}`).
`provision` is a generated mutation handle or `{name}`, including qualified names such as `accounts.provision`. The returned records
contain email, password, principal, token and expiresAt, grouped by role.
`startServe(dir, {seedUsers: options})` performs the same setup before returning
and exposes those records as `sessions`. Before minting or creating accounts,
the helper requires environment=staging and development=false. Production,
legacy and dev hosts refuse. Inputs are validated before effects; signup is
sequential, bounded, respects identity throttling, and never retries an ambiguous
write. A fresh call creates a fresh random email/password set. Partial failure
does not claim rollback: some accounts/grants may exist; discard the disposable
staging deployment or inspect it before retrying. Application data is created
through ordinary authenticated mutations after provisioning.

Credential records are returned to the operator, never logged by the helper.
The tested guide writes them to an exclusively created 0600 file. They must
not enter source control or reports. There is no public provisioning HTTP
endpoint beyond the application's declared rule-checked mutation.

## 3. First admin

The tested guide uses password signup (which grants no role), then the
filesystem owner's `operatorToken()` to invoke an operator-only mutation.
The roster's insert rule independently requires service:operator. No "first
caller wins", empty-roster bypass, client-selected signup role, or permanent
operator credential in the frontend. The same recipe works on production
with explicit operator-selected email/password; bulk seedAccounts refuses there.
Privileged account tokens cannot mint service tokens. SEC owns lints for
self-bootstrapped global authority; the guide points to this ownership.

## 4. Development doors

For password-only schemas (`auth.password && !auth.guests`), dev disables
`/seed`, every `/dev/*` door (except the existing cryptographically protected
local token protocol), and persona headers by default. The pre-existing serve
GET /dev/latency inspection remains service-authenticated; it never admits an
unauthenticated caller and its reset remains refused. `dev
--unsafe-dev-doors` is explicit opt-in with a prominent warning; serve accepts
no such flag. Host/Origin loopback fences still apply. Door availability is
computed from the current adopted schema, so hot adoption to password-only
also closes them. Seed/reset, clock advance and dev job enqueue revalidate
against the engine schema under the writer immediately before privileged effects;
slow request bodies and requests queued behind adoption cannot retain authority.
Action admission/replay, session-route admission, persona cancellation and upload
owner state transitions likewise revalidate under their actual writer. Previously
admitted durable work retains the existing work-record contract; a refused
new request creates no claimable work.
Persona reads also revalidate against the engine used to evaluate the query,
sync page or asset grant, checking the current declared cast at that read’s
admission. In-flight reads retain their existing snapshot semantics: cast
publication does not lock out concurrent ordinary writes, and the engine
transaction rejects a replaced execution schema.
Change-poll presence entry revalidates under its engine. A detached old
schema is fenced by the engine transaction; a replacement password-only reader
cannot inherit a pre-adoption persona capability. A persona header must name an explicitly declared persona;
an empty declaration admits none. Persona-based schemas retain their ordinary
development workflow. /auth/config always reports development=true on dev,
even with closed doors, so probe tooling can refuse it.

`startDev` follows native persistent storage by default, consuming the old
--no-memory alias; --memory/--fresh explicitly request disposable storage.
The returned now() refuses with guidance if the clock door is closed. Native
readiness plus the per-launch proof marker still establish host identity when
/dev/status is unavailable. Existing fixture/clock tests explicitly opt into
unsafe dev doors when their password schema requires those tools. Generated
frontend proofs explicitly select --memory and --unsafe-dev-doors, preserving
disposable fixture isolation and repeatability under the persistent helper
default. Exact 0.4.30/0.4.31 proof templates are retained and safely adapted
by digest; custom scripts remain untouched. DAY5 owns other starter custody.

## 5. Evidence

Required: production relabelling refusal before writes; staging retention over
hot/cold release switches; real signup/login per role and operator-only grants;
self-grant and unauthenticated doors refused; default/explicit dev doors and
schema-adoption closure; persistent/default and disposable dev; private token
logs; the exact guide recipe executed from the packed tarball in Linux
qualification, including production bulk-seed refusal and first admin; three
copied wave-16 dev probes converted to serve. Full crate tests, affected client
tests, Darwin affected tests on the assigned Mac Studio, ref-check, docs budget
and root inventory/guide checks. Never use the full scripts/test.sh here;
qualify-linux --consumer-only complements the manually run crate suites.

## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.

### Session input and compatibility

Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.

### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries

ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.

For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
deadlines/backoffs remain business time.

Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
bearer's matching request URL/header and monotonically increases its live
expiry/cap before clock listeners run. Local/device clients await durable
credential custody before publishing or persisting their business clock.
Online clients keep a volatile clock; their existing session listeners may
persist custody asynchronously. Authenticated restoration still validates
expired metadata with the staging probe; no online durability barrier is implied.
Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
local/device clock publication are serialized: durable credential saves are awaited
before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
auth operation or remote revocation queue.
Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
Retention preserves a decoded body, not a stale authentication classification.
An E_AUTH refusal remains scoped to the bearer revision actually dispatched:
rotation supersedes prior and intermediate retiring-bearer revisions, including
when the response was decoded before rotation or arrives after cancellation or
a retryable refresh failure. Recheck that authority when consuming retained
responses. A successor already dispatched during credential persistence remains
current; its own refusal may sign it out. Sign-out alone does not supersede a
same-bearer refusal, and sent outcomes and business refusals retain their ordinary
invocation custody. Retryable refresh failure still permits a same-id retry under
the current credential revision.
Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.

advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.

A saved boundary is future-held only when it is strictly greater than the
boundary of the requested effective schedule window. Equality means that the
current window was already processed: report not-due, without consulting wall
time. Repeated advances inside that window and zero-time drains succeed without
allowHeld, including recovery of queued work after a failed drain completion.
Never enqueue the processed window again.
A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
schedule, saved boundary, next unprocessed window and recovery duration to
reach the saved boundary from the unchanged process clock, not from the rejected
requested time. Relative recovery hints in accepted reports likewise use the
actual process clock, including when a disclosure floor is ahead of it.
A held report sets heldUntil to that saved boundary and
nextBoundary to the next unprocessed boundary. Catching up to heldUntil
reports not-due and never re-enqueues the processed window; reaching nextBoundary
fires once. Fresh staging storage and continuing with the original offset are
recovery choices; saved markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.

### Upgrade advice and future formats

Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
guide changes remains available. No ancestor
process inspection or script mutation is introduced.

The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.

### Starter and proof rendering

Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and

selection and explicit web witness/generated API imports. The proof driver installs the
existing witness bridge before app creation; createApp calls an immutable Symbol observer only under explicit witness=web.
This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication
boundary. A witness URL alone installs no observer and exposes no App global.
The driver installs its nonconfigurable/nonwritable observer before application
scripts and locks/freezes the selected witness bridge; the first App remains
selected for that page. Same-App explicit API registration can enrich it;
a different explicit App refuses E_WITNESS_APP_SELECTION and requires a separate
page. Later automatic Apps cannot silently redirect the proof. Application JS
remains trusted to implement the application: same-origin code can forge its
own test observer outside a driven page, just as it can read web session storage.
The observer grants no new credentials or backend authority. Ordinary bundles
carry only the creation dispatch, not the witness implementation. No-API
registration captures only durable non-ephemeral mutation handles; direct
witness mutate still requires generated API.

Proof text locators match normalized entire descendant text, including composed
React Native spans and wrapping labels. Choose smallest matching visible,
non-editable elements; independent matches retain strict Playwright ambiguity.
Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,
with no Unicode normalization or input value matching. Exact strings are case-sensitive;
explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
Text ranges outside overflow clips do not contribute evidence to a visible
ancestor. Layoutless wrappers may forward their visible descendants; a clipped
suffix cannot manufacture a complete status label.

## 12. Wave-24 loop repairs (DX7)

Commission: Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22; implementer: Codex in sb4-b24-dx7.
This amends §11, LLP 3000.036 §22.8 and the ordinary rule-helper exclusion.
SEC8 owns security questionnaire/dispositions, presence intent, invariant test
coverage and lifecycle advice; DX7 only reports their existing verdicts.
Implementation and tests accompany this amendment; review readiness is distinct
from author acceptance.

### Durable staging time

A staging store owns its cumulative offset and latest explicitly checkpointed
business time. The additive typed metadata record also retains a pending
maintenance pause. Production ignores this record and rejects clock controls;
ordinary dev retains its process-local clock/reset contract. No release-format
change or filesystem sidecar is needed. Store adapters use their existing
metadata transaction and fencing, including Postgres.

Startup resumes at the maximum of wall plus saved offset, checkpointed time,
and the existing disclosure floor. Without a checkpoint, the latest retained
commit/schedule boundary supplies the legacy recovery floor. Explicit startup
offsets are absolute offsets from wall time, clamped to the resumed floor;
restarting never adds the same offset twice or rewinds saved boundaries.
The resulting effective offset is persisted at startup. Malformed checkpoints
refuse startup rather than silently resetting. Downgrades to older binaries
ignore this additive record and retain their historical process-local behavior.

Each accepted staging advance checkpoints offset, time and paused=true in the
same transaction that preserves eligible sessions and worker leases, before
publishing the process clock or doing maintenance. A storage failure rolls back
all those effects. A lost reply is still ambiguous and never automatically
replayed. drain:false, a failed drain and an interrupted drain retain the pause
across restart. A successful drain durably clears it only after due work has
finished. If that final write fails, report an incomplete drain and retain the
pause. A restart does not shift already-preserved credentials again. Clock
status/advance reports say the offset belongs to this staging store. Coalescing,
eachBoundary, current-window equality and explicit allowHeld keep §11 semantics.

### Rendered and scrollable text

Mounted text inside overflow:auto/scroll ancestors counts even when outside
the scrollport: it can be reached by scrolling. The selector does not scroll
or change application layout. Overflow:hidden/clip remains a real clip, with
character geometry retaining only the displayed prefix; display:none,
visibility:hidden/collapse, opacity:0 and content-visibility:hidden remain
excluded, as do editable/input/script text and layoutless text. This does not
claim occlusion detection or virtualized content that is not mounted. Existing
normalization, smallest matching element and strict ambiguity remain unchanged.

### Upgrade and gate presentation

Upgrade snapshots count security notes alongside compiler notes and report
pending review gates separately, with unavailable previous gate data stated
honestly for old snapshots. The gate status reflects acknowledgments without
writing them during reporting. A refuted invariant cannot be acknowledged:
check explicitly reports that --ack-security was not applied, leaves review
records untouched and explains that the policy/intent must be repaired.
The JSON result carries the same explanation. Gate-only upgrade failures name
check --ack-security <ID> --reason '<spec rationale>'; other failures retain
schema/device remediation. An already published old CLI may still print its
old E_UPGRADE line; the new check child must carry the actionable explanation.
The release card records the 0.4.37 CLI's obsolete closed-door/startDev advice.
The numeric-advance candidate scan requires an actual advance call in the same
local expression/assignment as numeric consumption; unrelated operators or
new Date/assert calls elsewhere in a file do not qualify.

### Protected immutable payloads

A column-read-protected payload may be immutable. On insert its supplied value
is validated normally. On every update/existing-upsert, a supplied protected
immutable field is ignored without comparing it with stored data, for every
viewer, including its readers and the system. Its retained value and asset
placement remain unchanged; absent-upsert still inserts. Compiler advice on an
explicit patch names that behavior. Ordinary unprotected immutability retains
its existing contract. Cap/unique/index/authority/derived dependencies on
protected fields remain refused. This input-independent policy preserves
LLP 3000.036 §22.8's noninterference oracle and needs no new device protocol:
the same interpreter runs it on the server and device.

### Audience helpers and hidden probes

Expression-bodied helpers, or a block containing one return, may appear in
table/column rules when expansion is exactly the existing rule grammar.
Arguments are ordinary typed rule terms, substituted simultaneously without
caller capture. Only parameters, viewer and rule constants may be free in the
helper; a helper's focal dot cannot capture the caller's row. Nested helpers
are bounded to eight levels and a bounded expanded-node budget; cycles,
wrong arity/types, block effects/lets, arithmetic, clock and ordinary reads
refuse with E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR and an actionable repair. No new runtime
instruction, probe semantics, authority or resource allowance is introduced.
Expansion precedes read-through, index inference, audience inversion and
security analysis so every consumer sees the same canonical predicate.

Program exists remains a caller-visible read; rule exists retains its existing
policy probe semantics. N_UNREADABLE_PROBE and N_LOOKUP_FILTERED name the exact
hiding read/read-through rule and source site, including exists directly in a
require. No runtime refusal confirms whether a hidden row physically exists.
Runnable guide recipes demonstrate protected immutable payloads, a role helper
and a hidden parent probe alongside a deliberately minimal readable projection.

### Required evidence

Regression coverage includes repeated startServe/advance/drain runs on one
store, drain:false restart and legacy saved boundaries; no double session
shift; production controls and failed-checkpoint atomicity; mounted below-fold
RN-web text and hidden/clip controls; gate-only and refuted upgrade diagnostics;
real and unrelated advance scan candidates; protected immutable equal/different
patches, upserts, assets and server/device observation equality; helper types,
recursion, capture and authority equivalence; hidden program exists source
advice. Every changed guide snippet executes against the fresh pack. Full
five-crate Rust tests, affected client pool, Mac Studio affected platform tests,
qualify-linux --consumer-only (test.sh is prohibited), published 0.4.35/0.4.37
old-CLI upgrades, refs/docs budget and repository-root checks are recorded in
WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md. No version bump, publication or push.

## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.

### Session input and compatibility

Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.

### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries

ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.

For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
deadlines/backoffs remain business time.

Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
bearer's matching request URL/header and monotonically increases its live
expiry/cap before clock listeners run. Local/device clients await durable
credential custody before publishing or persisting their business clock.
Online clients keep a volatile clock; their existing session listeners may
persist custody asynchronously. Authenticated restoration still validates
expired metadata with the staging probe; no online durability barrier is implied.
Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
local/device clock publication are serialized: durable credential saves are awaited
before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
auth operation or remote revocation queue.
Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
Retention preserves a decoded body, not a stale authentication classification.
An E_AUTH refusal remains scoped to the bearer revision actually dispatched:
rotation supersedes prior and intermediate retiring-bearer revisions, including
when the response was decoded before rotation or arrives after cancellation or
a retryable refresh failure. Recheck that authority when consuming retained
responses. A successor already dispatched during credential persistence remains
current; its own refusal may sign it out. Sign-out alone does not supersede a
same-bearer refusal, and sent outcomes and business refusals retain their ordinary
invocation custody. Retryable refresh failure still permits a same-id retry under
the current credential revision.
Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.

advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical

### 22.8 Exact admission and observation boundary (round-one clarification)

The supported runtime grammar is **exactly the existing read-rule grammar**:
allow/deny/public, equality/inequality over own ordinary fields/viewer/literals,
and/or/not and unique readable `exists`. `created`, ordered comparisons,
old/next image operands and reference terms are not column-read forms. A
reference-derived audience is written as an existing unique `exists` probe.
The row-local subfragment excludes `exists` entirely. No column gate may use
any field protected by either a column rule or owner-private authority, even
when another branch would establish ownership. Rule-term validation recursively
walks every Boolean arm and every probe key and residual target field, using
the bound target index's actual columns. A raw schema gets the same walk.

**Noninterference oracle:** fix schema, viewer, arguments, clock, public rows
and all policy-selector/witness values. Vary only a column's stored payload,
with its effective rule false in both worlds. Every supported application
observation (data, refusal, meter, completeness, continuation and dependency
table names) must be equal. This includes absent-vs-present-null whole-row
shapes, explicit scalars, null filters, count/exists, computed group/sort and
writes. Projecting every hidden payload to the same absent/null observation
satisfies this oracle; the public fact that the viewer is denied is not a
promise to conceal the rule or to simulate an authorized null value. Blind
writes are deliberately governed by row write authority, just as readable
fields are; apps needing narrower writes also declare `written by` or narrower
row write rules. Immutable/cap/unique/after-insert rules cannot use protected
payloads because refusal differences would test guesses; input-only text/type
validation remains legal. No existing schema without column rules changes.

The structural dependency census also includes: all timeline mappings and
predicates, receipt declarations, every maintained predicate (including
row-keyed member-side predicates), engine captures through descendants,
recorded-attribution sources, generated contribution indexes and source
sequences. A protected cell may not appear anywhere inside a rule's reference
path. Protecting a *previously* unprotected selector is checked against the
entire new schema, including already-declared child captures. Such an adoption
is invalid before storage is touched. A protected maintained output is admitted
only when it has no downstream structural users; its derivation inputs still
obey the input refusal. In-memory sort/group consumes only projected values;
physical index ordering on protected values always refuses.

**Delivery transaction:** shared pending/log images omit every column-protected
payload, even in principal partitions. Snapshot acquisition and stream serving
use their existing read transaction and re-fetch the current stored row, test
row authority, and evaluate its row-local column rules for the recipient. They
already serve current images rather than historical put bodies. Selector changes
are projected from that same current image; no independent cell log or audience
is introduced. Server-witness cells are never delivered. A device re-applies
row-local projection before pricing, returning or rebuilding defaults. Server-
witness tables are conservatively server-class for *all* application read sites,
including projections without the field; this is an intentional documented
availability tradeoff, not a claim of cell-level residency analysis. Any
mutation writing one queues without prediction; a held query with such a site
refuses `E_COLUMN_READ`. Ordinary online fallback needs no SDK policy branch.

Schema/generation replacement follows the existing device installation reset:
no old images publish under the new generation before it is installed and its
partitions acquired. This applies to adding/removing a gate and to changing
between row-local and server-witness rules. Old offline clients can retain
previously disclosed bytes (the same ordinary revocation boundary as rows);
servers never deliver newly protected bytes to an old decoder. No claim of
retroactive erasure is made for delivered history or offline clients.

Live invalidation uses the existing `Runner::rule_dependencies` and response
`tables` envelope. Every read registers the table's full column-rule witness
closure independently of evaluated arms, including empty reads. The existing
live-query dependency machinery observes those tables; no new invalidation
index or write-time fanout is needed. Probe deadlines use the existing scoped
expiry machinery; all branches prepay their static probe/scratch bounds.
Column-bearing tables cannot use actual raw-size pricing fast paths. Only
row+column-authorized results can be priced at actual payload length.

Asset denial precedes range handling and one-view consumption; a denied caller
gets the same unknown-asset envelope as an unowned id, whether the column is
scalar or an asset list. Placement remains insert/update authority plus the
existing one-home law; it confers no read authority. There are no thumbnails
or transformed asset paths in this product.

Type emission covers Rows, baseline/write rows, row shapes/objects, explicit
projections, spreads and named views. Write *input* fields retain their declared
requiredness: read optionality is not optional input. The old-client report
names an existing required field becoming optional when its read rule is added.
Old already-generated code cannot be rewritten by the server; the preview says
that it must handle omission. An intentional rollback to a wider audience keeps
the existing confidentiality warning; a new hard approval gate is not part of
this commission's normal-adoption requirement.

Audit prints the actual effective conjunction and residency per column and
includes grant writers reached from column probes. The side-table note is a
conservative advisory, only for an ordinary table with exactly one required
parent reference covered by a single-column unique key and a nonidentical read
rule; it never asserts equivalence or rewrites data automatically. The five
copied migrations explicitly backfill the new column and remove obsolete side-
table write paths; their comparison records supply the cutover evidence.

Qualification thresholds are those commissioned: Rust core/lang/CLI/sim/device/
difftest suites and full client pool all pass; `run` seeds 0–19999,
`run-devices` seeds 0–999 on SQLite and memory, and `run-lean` seeds 0–19999
introduce zero new signatures; Lean builds/checks with no sorry/new axioms;
the 200 original schemas (100 wave 15, 50 wave 16, 50 wave 18) acquire zero new
refusals; packed guide examples run unchanged; five lane copies verify row
visibility at rollback, private payload denial, allowed payloads and restored
forward cells. Unsupported SEC3 proof paths remain explicitly Unproved; they
are not hard refusals unless the schema itself violates admission above.


### 22.9 Blind asset assignment and device acquisition (Codex round one)

For every explicitly supplied asset or asset-list field whose *old cell* is
not readable by the caller, placement must require uploader ownership even
when the supplied id equals a hidden old id. It uses the existing blind-row
placement check at cell granularity. Omitted cells are retained without a new
placement authorization test. Paired tests submit an equal versus unequal
non-owned known asset id and require identical outcome and meter. Protected
immutable payloads are rejected by the §22.8 admission census.

A device cannot infer an omitted cell's value by making its selector grant
access. For every predicted insert/update/upsert on a column-bearing table,
if an unsupplied protected field would change from denied/omitted to allowed,
the prediction queues without a row. No default or null fills the gap, even
when the stored type is optional. Server settlement plus recipient projection
acquires the actual value. A supplied value can predict only when its read
policy is row-local and all ordinary write/prediction checks pass. Tests cover
selector grant, unchanged denial, ordinary private patch, and explicit supply
on both device stores.

Acceptance also covers column-policy grant/revoke/expiry without a data-row
edit; both row-local ↔ server-witness generation transitions with outstanding
predictions; and optionality through spreads, transient views, baseline and
write-result types. The RFC review record is not a claim these tests have run.

//! Bounded, read-only evidence from the store's own commit clock.
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

const SKIPPED_PREVIEW: usize = 32;
const TOLERANCE_MS: i64 = 5_000;
const RECENT_COMMITS: usize = 64;
const TABLE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
const TABLE_NAMES: usize = 8;
const REPORT_ERROR_BYTES: usize = 1024;
// Reserve one MiB for the outer clock/work envelope inside the host encoder.
// The reply retains `schedules` and its fired/held partition.
const REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET: usize = (crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING - (1 << 20)) / 2;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — inspect a fixed recent commit window, never application row values.
pub fn ahead(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
    // Reverse primary-key traversal: no full scan, sort, row payloads or retained
    // historical stamp set. octet_length(column) uses SQLite record metadata;
    // unlike a text length/cast/substr, it need not load oversized payloads.
    let mut lead = 0;
    let mut tables = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut omitted = false;
    engine.store().visit_recent_commit_clock(now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS), TABLE_BYTES as i64, RECENT_COMMITS as i64, |record| {
        let at = record.at;
        if at <= now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS) { return Ok(()); }
        lead = lead.max(at.saturating_sub(now));
        let length = record.length.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("commit clock record is missing touched length".into()))?;
        if length > TABLE_BYTES as i64 { omitted = true; return Ok(()); }
        let bytes = record.touched.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("commit clock record is missing touched bytes".into()))?;
        match serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<String>>(&bytes) {
            Ok(names) => for name in names {
                if tables.contains(&name) { continue; }
                if tables.len() < TABLE_NAMES && name.len() <= 128 { tables.insert(name); }
                else { omitted = true; }
            },
            Err(_) => omitted = true,
        }
        Ok(())
    })?;
    if lead == 0 { return Ok(None); }
    let mut names = tables.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if omitted { names.push("additional tables omitted".into()); }
    if names.is_empty() { names.push("no table names recorded".into()); }
    Ok(Some(format!(
        "N_CLOCK_STORE_AHEAD: recent commit stamps lead the current clock by up to {lead}ms (latest {RECENT_COMMITS} commits; tables: {}); use a fresh store per offset test ({}), or restart with the same --clock-offset (or dev --resume-clock) to continue",
        names.join(", "), crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())))
}

/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
}

/// A positive duration in the units `clock advance` accepts, rounded up to a second.
pub fn span(ms: i64) -> String {
    let seconds = (ms.max(0) + 999) / 1_000;
    let (d, h, m, s) = (seconds / 86_400, seconds % 86_400 / 3_600, seconds % 3_600 / 60, seconds % 60);
    let parts: Vec<String> = [(d, "d"), (h, "h"), (m, "m"), (s, "s")].into_iter().filter(|(n, _)| *n > 0).map(|(n, unit)| format!("{n}{unit}")).collect();
    if parts.is_empty() { "0s".into() } else { parts.join("") }
}

/// Each schedule's saved boundary, in declaration order.
pub fn saved_boundaries(engine: &Engine) -> Vec<Option<i64>> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter()
        .map(|schedule| {
            let shape = engine.store().schedule_shape(&schedule.name).ok().flatten();
            if shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|shape| *shape != snapback4_core::value::digest(schedule)) { return None; }
            engine.store().schedule_boundary(&schedule.name).ok().flatten()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Preflight is bounded before the clock or worker leases change.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — only explicit execution enumerates all crossed windows; coalesced reports keep a bounded preview.
pub fn crossed_boundaries(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool) -> Result<Vec<(usize, i64)>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    let mut boundaries = Vec::new();
    let mut report_bytes = 0usize;
    for (index, schedule) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate() {
        // JSON may escape every error byte; count that bound per schedule.
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add(2048 + 6 * (REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3) + 8 * (schedule.name.len() + schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule report exceeds its byte budget; reduce the declared schedules")); }
        if held { continue; }
        let Some(old) = before.get(index).copied().flatten() else { continue; };
        let end = schedule.boundary(now);
        if old >= end { continue; }
        let periods = schedule.periods_between(old, end);
        if each_boundary && periods > (10_000 - boundaries.len()) as i64 {
            return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("--each-boundary crosses more than 10000 schedule windows; use a smaller duration or omit --each-boundary to coalesce"));
        }
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add((if each_boundary { periods as usize } else { (periods as usize).min(SKIPPED_PREVIEW + 1) }).saturating_mul(1024 + 8 * schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule window report exceeds its byte budget; use a smaller duration")); }
        if !each_boundary { continue; }
        let mut boundary = schedule.next(old);
        while boundary <= end {
            boundaries.push((index, boundary));
            boundary = schedule.next(boundary);
        }
    }
    boundaries.sort_by_key(|(index, at)| (*at, *index));
    Ok(boundaries)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — no silent successful advance behind retained schedule markers.
pub fn refuse_held(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], current_clock: i64, now: i64) -> Result<(), snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    for (schedule, saved) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(before) {
        // Equality is the already processed current window, not a hold. The
        // authoritative requested clock defines the window, never wall time.
        if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| *saved > schedule.boundary(now)) {
            return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_HELD", "clock", format!(
                "schedule {} already processed boundary {}; requested clock {} is in an earlier window; next unprocessed boundary is {}. Nothing advanced. Advance {} to reach the saved window or use a fresh staging deployment; allowHeld:true explicitly accepts this hold. Never rewind saved boundaries",
                schedule.name, utc(saved), utc(now), utc(schedule.next(saved)), format!("{}ms", saved.saturating_sub(current_clock)))).guide("clock"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn period(schedule: &snapback4_core::schema::Schedule) -> String {
    schedule.describe()
}

/// What each schedule did on one clock advance, and why one did not fire.
/// The core fires each schedule at most once per advance, for the latest
/// boundary, and holds it while its saved boundary is ahead of the clock.
// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — missed boundaries fire once; this only explains them.
pub fn schedule_report(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], fired: &[String], now: i64, current_clock: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool, port: Option<u16>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let after = saved_boundaries(engine);
    // Read only bounded summaries: job args/cursors and full error payloads
    // are irrelevant to this report and must not be loaded then replicated.
    let runs = job_summaries(engine).unwrap_or_default();
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| {
        let (old, saved) = (before.get(index).copied().flatten(), after.get(index).copied().flatten());
        let current = schedule.boundary(now);
        let next = schedule.next(current);
        let mut entry = serde_json::json!({ "name": schedule.name, "target": schedule.target, "period": period(schedule), "fired": false, "firedWindows": [], "skippedBoundaries": [], "nextBoundary": utc(next) });
        if fired.contains(&schedule.name) {
            let end = saved.unwrap_or(current);
            entry["fired"] = true.into();
            let start = schedule.previous(end);
            let window = |boundary| serde_json::json!({"periodStart": schedule.previous(boundary), "periodEnd": boundary});
            let mut windows = Vec::new();
            if each_boundary {
                if let Some(old) = old {
                    let mut at = schedule.next(old);
                    while at <= end { windows.push(window(at)); at = schedule.next(at); }
                }
            } else { windows.push(window(end)); }
            if each_boundary {
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired {} windows: {}", windows.len(), windows.iter().map(|window| format!("{} to {}", utc(window["periodStart"].as_i64().unwrap()), utc(window["periodEnd"].as_i64().unwrap()))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ")).into();
            }
            entry["firedWindows"] = windows.into();
            entry["periodStart"] = start.into();
            entry["periodEnd"] = end.into();
            if !each_boundary { entry["reason"] = format!("fired for the period {} to {}", utc(start), utc(end)).into(); }
            if let Some(run) = runs.get(&schedule.target) { entry["run"] = run.clone(); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.040#24-monthly-and-yearly-schedules — calendar periods count boundaries, not milliseconds.
            let skipped = if each_boundary { 0 } else { old.map(|old| schedule.periods_between(old, end) - 1).unwrap_or(0) };
            if skipped > 0 {
                entry["skippedPeriods"] = skipped.into();
                let mut windows = Vec::new();
                let mut at = schedule.next(old.unwrap());
                while at < end && windows.len() < SKIPPED_PREVIEW {
                    let mut item = window(at);
                    let mut args = serde_json::Map::new();
                    if let Some(program) = engine.program(&schedule.target) {
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") { args.insert("periodStart".into(), schedule.previous(at).into()); }
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") { args.insert("periodEnd".into(), at.into()); }
                    }
                    item["command"] = format!("snapback4 run {} '{}'{}", schedule.target, serde_json::Value::Object(args), port.map(|port| format!(" --port {port}")).unwrap_or_default()).into();
                    windows.push(item); at = schedule.next(at);
                }
                entry["skippedBoundariesOmitted"] = (skipped - windows.len() as i64).into();
                entry["skippedBoundaries"] = windows.into();
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired once, for the latest period {} to {}; {skipped} earlier period{} this advance crossed (from {}) did not run: missed boundaries fire once. Run {} with periodStart/periodEnd for an earlier period",
                    utc(start), utc(end), if skipped == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, utc(old.unwrap_or(end)), schedule.target).into();
            }
        } else if held {
            entry["holdCode"] = "disabled".into();
            entry["reason"] = "schedules are held (dev --hold-schedules or --replay); a restart without the flag resumes at the next boundary".into();
        } else if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| old.is_some() && *saved > current) {
            let due = schedule.next(saved);
            entry["holdCode"] = "saved-boundary".into();
            entry["savedBoundary"] = saved.into();
            entry["heldUntil"] = utc(saved).into();
            entry["nextBoundary"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("held by the store: boundary {} was already processed and this clock {} is in an earlier window (restarting resets the process offset, not the saved boundary). One fire per boundary. Advance {} more to reach the saved window, or use a fresh staging deployment/store for an independent test; keep the same --clock-offset when continuing a test across serve restarts",
                utc(saved), utc(now), span(saved.saturating_sub(current_clock))).into();
        } else if old != saved {
            entry["holdCode"] = "initialized".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("{} started at boundary {}: a schedule fires at the boundary after the first one it sees, next {} ({} from now)",
                if old.is_none() { "this schedule" } else { "this changed schedule" }, utc(saved.unwrap_or(current)), utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        } else {
            entry["holdCode"] = "not-due".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("next boundary {} ({} from now; schedule times are UTC)", utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        }
        entry
    }).collect()
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — every declared schedule has one reported outcome.
pub fn outcomes(schedules: &[serde_json::Value]) -> (Vec<serde_json::Value>, Vec<serde_json::Value>) {
    schedules.iter().cloned().partition(|schedule| schedule["fired"] == true)
}

/// The report never loads full error/argument payloads from retained jobs.
fn job_summaries(engine: &Engine) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut summaries = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for summary in engine.store().job_summaries(REPORT_ERROR_BYTES)? {
        let name = summary.name;
        if summaries.contains_key(&name) { continue; }
        let mut error = summary.error;
        let truncated = summary.error_truncated;
        if let Some(text) = &mut error && truncated {
            let mut end = REPORT_ERROR_BYTES.min(text.len());
            while !text.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }
            text.truncate(end); text.push('…');
        }
        summaries.insert(name, serde_json::json!({ "id":summary.id, "state":summary.state,
            "rowsWritten":summary.rows_written, "error":error, "errorTruncated":truncated }));
    }
    Ok(summaries)
}

/// Startup lines for schedules the store holds: their saved boundary leads the clock.
pub fn held_schedules(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Vec<String> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(saved_boundaries(engine)).filter_map(|(schedule, saved)| {
        let saved = saved.filter(|saved| *saved > schedule.boundary(now))?;
        let due = schedule.next(saved);
        Some(format!("clock     schedule {} is held until {} ({} from now): catch up to its saved boundary; next unprocessed window {}; `clock advance {}` or restart with dev --resume-clock",
            schedule.name, utc(saved), span(saved - now), utc(due), format!("{}ms", saved - now)))
    }).collect()
}

/// The dev clock offset that continues a store's own time: its newest
/// recent commit stamp (or saved schedule boundary) less wall time, never negative.
pub fn resume_offset(store: &snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore, wall: i64) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
    let commit = store.recent_commit_max_at(RECENT_COMMITS as i64)?;
    let boundary = store.latest_schedule_boundary()?;
    let latest = commit.into_iter().chain(boundary).max().unwrap_or(wall);
    // Whole seconds, rounded up, so restarting twice does not drift backwards.
    Ok((latest.saturating_sub(wall).max(0) + 999) / 1_000 * 1_000)
}

pub fn has_data(engine: &Engine) -> bool {
    engine.store().inspection_has_data().unwrap_or(false)
}

pub fn offset_line(offset: i64, running: bool) -> String {
    format!("clock     offset from wall time: {offset:+}ms{}", if running { " (lasts until restart)" } else { " (no running dev; inspecting against wall time)" })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    fn engine() -> Engine {
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), "table alpha:\n  at: time\n  public\ntable beta:\n  at: time\n  public\n".into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema,
            bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program), 100_000).unwrap()
    }
    fn seed(engine: &mut Engine, table: &str, commit_at: i64, row_at: i64) {
        engine.seed_at([(table.into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
            ("id", snapback4_core::Value::Id(snapback4_core::ids::mint(row_at, &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).unwrap())),
            ("at", snapback4_core::Value::Int(row_at)),
        ]))], commit_at).unwrap();
    }
    #[test]
    fn clock_report_bounds_one_large_job_error_repeated_across_many_schedules() {
        let mut source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\n".to_owned();
        for n in 0..500 { source.push_str(&format!("schedule s{n} every 1m: tick\n")); }
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let mut engine = Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program), 0).unwrap();
        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();
        let before = saved_boundaries(&engine);
        assert_eq!(crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, 60_000, false, true).unwrap().len(), 500);
        let fired = engine.fire_schedules(60_000).unwrap();
        let message = "🧪\n\\".repeat(30_000);
        (engine.store()).test_support_conn().execute("UPDATE _jobs SET error = ?1 WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM _jobs ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1)", [&message]).unwrap();
        let report = schedule_report(&engine, &before, &fired, 60_000, 60_000, false, false, None);
        assert_eq!(report.len(), 500);
        assert!(report.iter().all(|s| s["run"]["errorTruncated"] == true));
        assert!(report.iter().all(|s| s["run"]["error"].as_str().unwrap().len() <= REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3));
        assert!(serde_json::to_vec(&report).unwrap().len() < 2 << 20);
    }
    #[test]
    fn clock_report_refuses_before_the_host_encoder_limit() {
        let mut source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\n".to_owned();
        for n in 0..3000 { source.push_str(&format!("schedule s{n} every 1m: tick\n")); }
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let mut engine = Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program), 0).unwrap();
        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();
        let before = saved_boundaries(&engine);
        let refusal = crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, 60_000, false, true).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_CLOCK_INPUT");
        assert!(refusal.message.contains("byte budget"));
        assert_eq!(before, saved_boundaries(&engine));
        assert!(REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET < crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING);
    }
    #[test]
    fn startup_hold_instruction_catches_up_without_repeating_the_saved_window() {
        let source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\nschedule hourly every 1h: tick\n";
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let mut engine = Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema,
            bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program), 0).unwrap();
        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();
        let saved = 5 * 3_600_000;
        engine.fire_schedules(saved).unwrap();
        let raw = 1_234;
        let lines = held_schedules(&engine, raw);
        assert_eq!(lines.len(), 1);
        let line = &lines[0];
        assert!(line.contains(&format!("held until {}", utc(saved))), "{line}");
        assert!(line.contains(&format!("next unprocessed window {}", utc(saved + 3_600_000))), "{line}");
        let duration = line.split_once("`clock advance ").unwrap().1.split_once('`').unwrap().0;
        let delta = crate::dev_clock::duration(duration).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(delta, saved - raw);
        let before = saved_boundaries(&engine);
        refuse_held(&engine, &before, raw, raw + delta).unwrap();
        assert!(engine.fire_schedules(raw + delta).unwrap().is_empty());
        assert!(held_schedules(&engine, raw + delta).is_empty());
        let report = schedule_report(&engine, &before, &[], raw + delta, raw + delta, false, false, None);
        assert_eq!(report[0]["holdCode"], "not-due");
        assert_eq!(engine.fire_schedules(saved + 3_600_000).unwrap(), vec!["hourly"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn utc_text_and_spans_match_the_calendar() {
        assert_eq!(utc(0), "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z");
        assert_eq!(utc(951_782_400_000), "2000-02-29T00:00:00Z");
        assert_eq!(utc(-1), "1969-12-31T23:59:59Z");
        assert_eq!(utc(1_791_468_000_000), "2026-10-08T14:00:00Z");
        assert_eq!(span(12_633_000), "3h30m33s");
        assert_eq!(span(86_400_001), "1d1s");
        assert_eq!(span(0), "0s");
    }
    #[test]
    fn resume_offset_follows_the_newest_commit_and_is_never_negative() {
        let mut engine = engine();
        assert_eq!(resume_offset(engine.store(), 100_000).unwrap(), 0);
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 3_700_500, 1);
        assert_eq!(resume_offset(engine.store(), 100_000).unwrap(), 3_601_000);
        assert_eq!(resume_offset(engine.store(), 9_000_000).unwrap(), 0);
    }
    #[test]
    fn commit_tolerance_and_largest_lead_ignore_future_application_values() {
        let mut engine = engine();
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 100_000, 1_000_000);
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().is_none());
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 105_000, 2_000_000);
        seed(&mut engine, "beta", 107_000, 3_000_000);
        let note = ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("up to 7000ms (latest 64 commits; tables: beta)"), "{note}");
        let note = ahead(&engine, 99_999).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("up to 7001ms (latest 64 commits; tables: alpha, beta)"), "{note}");
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 102_000).unwrap().is_none());
    }
    #[test]
    fn recent_window_does_not_claim_older_commits_or_read_row_payloads() {
        let mut engine = engine();
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 200_000, 200_000);
        for n in 0..RECENT_COMMITS { seed(&mut engine, "beta", 100_000, 300_000 + n as i64); }
        // Deliberately unreadable images: metadata inspection must not deserialize them.
        (engine.store()).test_support_conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data = 'not json'", []).unwrap();
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().is_none());
        (engine.store()).test_support_conn().execute("UPDATE _commits SET at = 200000, touched = ?1 WHERE seq = (SELECT MAX(seq) FROM _commits)", ["x".repeat(TABLE_BYTES + 1)]).unwrap();
        let note = ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("100000ms") && note.contains("additional tables omitted"), "{note}");
    }
}
//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

pub(crate) const PRESERVED_SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Staging sessions keep their remaining lifetime across this jump; sessions:expire explicitly tests credential expiry. Unplaced uploads still age. Never replay an ambiguous advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        let draining = options.positionals == ["drain"];
        if !draining && (options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance") {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        let duration_text = if draining { "0ms" } else { options.positionals[1].as_str() };
        if !draining { duration(duration_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; }
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else { let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?; (address,instance,None) };
        let mut body = serde_json::json!({"duration":duration_text,"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary"), "drain":!options.flags.contains_key("no-drain"), "allowHeld":options.flags.contains_key("allow-held")});
        if options.flags.contains_key("expire-sessions") { body["sessions"] = "expire".into(); }
        if draining && options.flags.contains_key("no-drain") { return Err(input("clock drain does not accept --no-drain").to_string()); }
        let body = body.to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if let Some(token) = &token {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,Some(token),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else { crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev(address, "/dev/clock/advance", instance.as_deref(), &body, Duration::from_secs(60)) };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            if json.get("now").is_some() {
                eprintln!("clock: incomplete advance report (time already moved): {}", serde_json::json!({"now":json["now"],"fired":json["fired"],"held":json["held"]}));
            }
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod isolated_tests {
    #[test]
    fn time_test_guidance_uses_only_valid_assigned_ranges_or_a_free_port() {
        assert_eq!(super::isolated_range(Some("24000"), Some("24009")), "dev --memory --port 24000-24009 within the current range");
        for (lo,hi) in [(None,None),(Some("0"),Some("3")),(Some("4"),Some("3")),(Some("bad"),Some("3"))] {
            assert_eq!(super::isolated_range(lo,hi), "dev --memory --port 0");
        }
    }
}
