    pub(super) fn update(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.device && (self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() || self.schema.tables[table_name].column_server_reads()) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
            ));
        }
        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
            runner.update_attempt(table_name, key, patch)
        })
    }

    fn update_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &patch, false)?;
        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &patch)?;
        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &patch)?;
        if patch.as_object()?.contains_key("id") {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} update patch cannot change id")));
        }
        let id = key.as_str()?;
        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &patch, false)?;
        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
        })? else {
            return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]));
        };
        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].sync.is_none() { return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])); }
        let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;
        self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &patch, copy)
    }

    pub(super) fn upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.device && (self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() || self.schema.tables[table_name].column_server_reads()) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
            ));
        }
        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
            runner.upsert_attempt(table_name, key, row)
        })
    }

    fn upsert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &row, false)?;
        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &row)?;
        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &row)?;
        let id = key.as_str()?;
        if row.field("id")?.as_str()? != id {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} upsert row id must equal its key")));
        }
        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &row, true)?;
        match self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
        })? {
            Some(old) => {
                let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
                let row = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, row, readable)?;
                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — an existing row receives a patch; omitted columns keep their values.
                let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &row, readable)?;
                self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &row, copy)
            }
            None if self.device && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])? =>
            {
                Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]))
            }
            None => self.insert_upsert(table_name, "byId", row),
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn insert_upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, addressed_index: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#5 — trusted fixture imports preserve the constraint layer.
        if self.context.is_system() {
            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| match error {
                RuntimeError::Input(message) => RuntimeError::Constraint(message),
                other => other,
            });
        }
        if self.schema.tables[table_name].through.is_some() {
            // A read-through child's insert arm keeps the hidden-target word for every authority refusal.
            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|e| match e {
                RuntimeError::Rule {..} | RuntimeError::Input(_) => self.no_write_target(), other => other,
            });
        }
        match self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()) {
            Err(RuntimeError::Input(_)) => Err(self.no_write_target()),
            result => result,
        }
    }

    fn replace(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.authorize_update_fields(table_name, &old, &new, patch, readable)?;
        self.replace_authorized(table_name, old, new, readable, patch, copy)
    }

    /// `copy` is the merged image's lawful price, charged again for an engine slot copy.
    pub(super) fn replace_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, patch, false)?;
        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, patch)?;
        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, patch)?;
        self.authorize_fields(table_name, &old, patch)?;
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
        for path in definition.columns.keys().filter(|field| {
            definition.engine_field(field) && field.as_str() != crate::schema::through::DEADLINE
        }) {
            if old.field(path).ok() != new.field(path).ok() {
                return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_RECORDED_FIELD", message: format!("engine replacement changed stored attribution at {table_name}.{path} (guide maintains)") } } else { self.no_write_target() });
            }
        }
        let mut new = new;
        self.schema.tables[table_name].recompute_deadline(&mut new)?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.017#2.2 — extending life re-admits the new image.
        if self.schema.tables[table_name].stamp_ephemeral(&mut new, self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?
            && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &new)? {
            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.into(), effect: Effect::Update } } else { self.no_write_target() });
        }
        if self.device {
            let table=&self.schema.tables[table_name];
            let hidden: Vec<_>=table.column_reads.keys().filter(|field|!table.local_column_readable(field,&new,Some(&self.context.viewer))).cloned().collect();
            if let Value::Row(fields)|Value::Map(fields)=&mut new { for field in hidden { fields.remove(&field); } }
        }
        let new = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, new, Some(&old), (!readable || !self.schema.tables[table_name].column_reads.is_empty()).then_some(patch))?;
        if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str())) { return Err(if readable { error } else { self.no_write_target() }); }
        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &new, Effect::Update)?;
        let new = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, Some(&old), new, copy)?;
        // A predicting device keeps another owner's omitted private field as an omission.
        super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str()))?;
        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        self.fixture_write(table_name, Effect::Update, Some(&old), Some(&new));
        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &new, Some(&old))
        })?;
        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), Some(&new), entries)?;
        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), Some(&new), Origin::Source)
    }

    pub(super) fn delete(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

//! E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR: a table rule uses an expression rules do not
//! evaluate (an ordered comparison outside insert rules and named update
//! transitions, the clock, arithmetic or a helper call). The rewrite moves the
//! author's own comparison into the mutation as `require … else CODE`.

use crate::ast::Expr;
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Site};

/// What the rule language lacks for this term, if anything.
pub(super) fn unsupported_side(expr: &Expr) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "now" => Some("the clock (`now`)"),
        Expr::Call { .. } => Some("a helper or function call"),
        Expr::Binary { op, .. } if matches!(op.as_str(), "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "%" | "??") => Some("arithmetic"),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The effect a rule judges, as the author spelled it.
pub(super) fn effect_word(insert: bool, update: bool, read: bool) -> &'static str {
    if insert { "insert" } else if update { "update" } else if read { "read" } else { "delete" }
}

/// The refusal for one comparison `cmp` in a `table`'s `effect` rule.
pub(super) fn diagnostic(site: &Site, table: &str, effect: &str, transition: bool, cmp: &Expr, what: &str) -> Diagnostic {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(cmp));
    let field = first_field(&text).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".to_owned());
    let code = format!("INVALID_{}", screaming(&field));
    let message = format!("`{text}` in the {effect} rule of {table} uses {what}, which table rules do not evaluate: rules compare columns, viewer and literals with = and !=, and order (<, <=, >, >=) only an insert row's own required int, time, decimal or money columns and integer literals (minor units beside decimal or money), or old/next in a named update (old, next) rule");
    // The mutation names the stored row `row` and supplies new values as arguments.
    let stored = |image: Option<&str>, name: &str| match image { Some("next") => name.to_owned(), _ => format!("row.{name}") };
    let inserted = |_: Option<&str>, name: &str| name.to_owned();
    let rewrite = match effect {
        "insert" => {
            let mutation = map_fields(&text, &inserted);
            if what == "an ordered comparison" {
                format!("compare this row's own required int or time columns or an integer literal in the insert rule, or check it in the mutation that inserts the row: `require {mutation} else {code}`")
            } else {
                format!("check it in the mutation that inserts the row, using the values it inserts: `require {mutation} else {code}`")
            }
        }
        "update" if !transition && what == "an ordered comparison" => {
            let next = map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("next.{name}"));
            format!("name both images and bound the new one: `update (old, next) <- {next}`; or check it in the mutation: `row = {table}[id] ! else NOT_FOUND` then `require {} else {code}`", map_fields(&text, &stored))
        }
        "read" if what.contains("now") => match direct_focal_field(cmp) {
            Some(expires) => format!("a read rule is an audience, which cannot change with time: hide rows past this row's stored time with `expire at .{expires}`, or filter the query (`{table} where {} …`)", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!(".{name}"))),
            None => format!("a read rule is an audience, which cannot change with time: copy the deciding deadline into a required time column on {table} and use `expire at .expiresAt`, or filter the query (`{table} where {} …`); `expire at` accepts a local time column, not a reference hop", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!(".{name}"))),
        },
        "read" => format!("a read rule is an audience, which cannot compare magnitudes: filter the query instead (`{table} where {} …`)", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!(".{name}"))),
        _ => format!("check it in the mutation before the write: `row = {table}[id] ! else NOT_FOUND` then `require {} else {code}`", map_fields(&text, &stored)),
    };
    Diagnostic::new(site, "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR", message, format!("{rewrite}; for counts/consent see: guide rule-recipes quantified-consent; for clock disclosure see: guide rule-recipes owner-now")).guide("rules")
}

/// An unnamed `update <- R` holds for the row before and after the write, so
/// its named form is `update (old, next) <- R(old) and R(next)`: every clause
/// kept, the ordered one included (lane 062). The mutation form follows.
pub(crate) fn named_update(table: &str, rule: &Expr, comparison: &str) -> String {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(rule));
    let wrap = |s: String| if text.contains(" or ") { format!("({s})") } else { s };
    let old = wrap(map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("old.{name}")));
    let next = wrap(map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("next.{name}")));
    let field = first_field(comparison).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".to_owned());
    let _ = table;
    format!("name both images; an unnamed update rule holds before and after the write, so the named form keeps both: `update (old, next) <- {old} and {next}`; or drop `{comparison}` from the rule and check the new value in the mutation: `require {} else INVALID_{}`", map_fields(comparison, &|_, name| name.to_owned()), screaming(&field))
}

/// Pasteable named form for a rule that already names one image. Bare focal
/// fields in a named transition refer to the new image.
pub(crate) fn named_update_source(rule: &Expr) -> String {
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — preserve authored old/next images and map bare fields to next in named transitions.
    let text = crate::print::expression(rule);
    let body = map_fields(&text, &|image, name| match image {
        Some(image) => format!("{image}.{name}"),
        None => format!("next.{name}"),
    });
    format!("update (old, next) <- {body}")
}

/// A named transition's comparison the rule language cannot type, as the
/// mutation check that states the same condition.
pub(crate) fn transition_require(table: &str, cmp: &Expr) -> String {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(cmp));
    let field = first_field(&text).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".to_owned());
    let stored = |image: Option<&str>, name: &str| match image { Some("next") => name.to_owned(), _ => format!("row.{name}") };
    format!("check it in the mutation that updates the row: `row = {table}[id] ! else NOT_FOUND` then `require {} else INVALID_{}` (the new values are the mutation's arguments)", map_fields(&text, &stored), screaming(&field))
}

/// A table rule's predicate as the check a mutation states before writing:
/// the row's fields become the values the mutation writes.
pub(crate) fn mutation_check(rule: &Expr) -> String {
    map_fields(&strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(rule)), &|_, name| name.to_owned())
}

/// `else CODE` after a table rule: the refusal of a rule is E_RULE.
pub(crate) fn rule_else(else_site: &Site, effect: &str, rule: &Expr, code: &str) -> Diagnostic {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(rule));
    let code = if code.chars().next().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase()) { code } else { "NOT_ALLOWED" };
    Diagnostic::new(else_site, "E_QUARRY_SYNTAX",
        format!("a table rule takes no `else`: a write its {effect} rule refuses is E_RULE; only `require … else CODE` and `unique … else CODE` name a refusal"),
        format!("keep `{effect} <- {text}`, and name the refusal in the mutation before the write: `require {} else {code}`", mutation_check(rule))).guide("rules")
}

fn strip_parens(text: &str) -> String {
    let trimmed = text.trim();
    if trimmed.starts_with('(') && trimmed.ends_with(')') {
        // Only strip a pair that encloses the whole text.
        let mut depth = 0i32;
        for (i, c) in trimmed.char_indices() {
            match c { '(' => depth += 1, ')' => depth -= 1, _ => {} }
            if depth == 0 && i + 1 < trimmed.len() { return trimmed.to_owned(); }
        }
        return trimmed[1..trimmed.len() - 1].to_owned();
    }
    trimmed.to_owned()
}

fn ident(c: char) -> bool { c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' }
fn ident_start(c: char) -> bool { c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '_' }

/// The first column the comparison names: `.stars`, `old.highBid` or `next.at`.
fn first_field(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    for (i, c) in chars.iter().enumerate() {
        if *c == '.' && chars.get(i + 1).is_some_and(|c| ident_start(*c)) {
            return Some(chars[i + 1..].iter().take_while(|c| ident(**c)).collect());
        }
    }
    None
}

/// A time field owned by the focal row. Do not descend through a member
/// chain: `.hearing.releaseAt` must never become `expire at .hearing`.
fn direct_focal_field(expr: &Expr) -> Option<&str> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Member { base, name, .. } if matches!(base.as_ref(), Expr::Focal { .. }) => Some(name),
        Expr::Binary { left, right, .. } => direct_focal_field(left).or_else(|| direct_focal_field(right)),
        Expr::Unary { value, .. } => direct_focal_field(value),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Rewrite each focal field `.f`, `old.f` and `next.f` through `map(image, f)`,
/// leaving other member accesses alone.
fn map_fields(text: &str, map: &dyn Fn(Option<&str>, &str) -> String) -> String {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let name_at = |at: usize| -> String { chars[at..].iter().take_while(|c| ident(**c)).collect() };
    while i < chars.len() {
        let c = chars[i];
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — field-looking text inside a literal is data, not a row-image reference.
        // Field-looking text inside a literal is data, not syntax. Preserve
        // the original spelling, including escaped quote characters.
        if matches!(c, '\'' | '"') {
            let quote = c;
            out.push(c);
            i += 1;
            while i < chars.len() {
                let literal = chars[i];
                out.push(literal);
                i += 1;
                if literal == '\\' && i < chars.len() {
                    out.push(chars[i]);
                    i += 1;
                } else if literal == quote {
                    break;
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        let previous = if i == 0 { None } else { Some(chars[i - 1]) };
        if c == '.' && previous.is_none_or(|p| !ident(p) && p != ')' && p != ']') && chars.get(i + 1).is_some_and(|c| ident_start(*c)) {
            let name = name_at(i + 1);
            out.push_str(&map(None, &name));
            i += 1 + name.chars().count();
            continue;
        }
        if ident(c) && previous.is_none_or(|p| !ident(p) && p != '.') {
            let word = name_at(i);
            let after = i + word.chars().count();
            if matches!(word.as_str(), "old" | "next") && chars.get(after) == Some(&'.') && chars.get(after + 1).is_some_and(|c| ident_start(*c)) {
                let name = name_at(after + 1);
                out.push_str(&map(Some(&word), &name));
                i = after + 1 + name.chars().count();
                continue;
            }
            out.push_str(&word);
            i = after;
            continue;
        }
        out.push(c);
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

fn screaming(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (i, c) in name.chars().enumerate() {
        if c.is_ascii_uppercase() && i > 0 { out.push('_'); }
        out.push(c.to_ascii_uppercase());
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn fields_move_into_the_mutation() {
        let stored = |image: Option<&str>, name: &str| match image { Some("next") => name.to_owned(), _ => format!("row.{name}") };
        assert_eq!(map_fields(".stars >= 1 and .stars <= 5", &|_, name| name.to_owned()), "stars >= 1 and stars <= 5");
        assert_eq!(map_fields("next.highBid >= old.highBid + old.increment", &stored), "highBid >= row.highBid + row.increment");
        assert_eq!(map_fields(".deadline > now", &stored), "row.deadline > now");
        assert_eq!(map_fields("helper(.a, viewer)", &stored), "helper(row.a, viewer)");
        assert_eq!(first_field("(old.highBid + 1)"), Some("highBid".into()));
        assert_eq!(screaming("drawAt"), "DRAW_AT");
        assert_eq!(strip_parens("(.a >= 1)"), ".a >= 1");
        assert_eq!(strip_parens("(.a) + (.b)"), "(.a) + (.b)");
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#11 — an explicit policy alternative, never an equivalent rewrite.
pub(crate) fn old_update_source(rule: &Expr) -> String {
    let text = crate::print::expression(rule);
    format!("update (old, next) <- {}", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("old.{name}")))
}
//! Proved contradictions between caller gates and table rules; unknown is quiet.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — bounded, path-local contradiction proofs never infer that different roles or principals are disjoint.
use super::catalog::Catalog;
use crate::{Diagnostic, ast::*};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

type Atom = (String, String, bool); // equality when true, inequality otherwise
// DNF: no alternatives is false; one empty alternative is unknown/true.
type Facts = Vec<Vec<Atom>>;
const LIMIT: usize = 64;
fn unknown() -> Facts {
    vec![vec![]]
}
fn combine(a: Facts, b: Facts, and: bool) -> Facts {
    if !and {
        return if a.len() + b.len() > LIMIT {
            unknown()
        } else {
            a.into_iter().chain(b).collect()
        };
    }
    if a.len().saturating_mul(b.len()) > LIMIT {
        return unknown();
    }
    a.into_iter()
        .flat_map(|a| b.iter().map(move |b| a.iter().chain(b).cloned().collect()))
        .collect()
}
fn possible(facts: &Facts) -> bool {
    facts.iter().any(|facts| {
        let mut roots = BTreeMap::<String, String>::new();
        fn root(roots: &BTreeMap<String, String>, term: &str) -> String {
            let mut at = term;
            while let Some(next) = roots.get(at) {
                at = next;
            }
            at.into()
        }
        for (a, b, equal) in facts {
            if !equal {
                continue;
            }
            let (a, b) = (root(&roots, a), root(&roots, b));
            if a != b {
                roots.insert(a, b);
            }
        }
        let mut literals = BTreeMap::new();
        for (a, b, _) in facts {
            for term in [a, b] {
                if term.starts_with("literal:") {
                    let r = root(&roots, term);
                    if let Some(old) = literals.insert(r, term)
                        && old != term
                    {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        facts
            .iter()
            .all(|(a, b, eq)| *eq || root(&roots, a) != root(&roots, b))
    })
}
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct Env {
    references: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    values: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    rows: BTreeMap<String, (String, BTreeMap<String, String>)>,
    gates: Vec<(String, Option<Vec<GateBranch>>)>,
}
// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#12 — positive caller probes prove physical probes;
// missing proof never means different roles are disjoint.
type Probe = (String, BTreeMap<String, String>);
#[derive(Clone)]
struct GateBranch { probes: Vec<Probe>, facts: Facts }
fn probe(catalog: &Catalog, expr: &Expr, env: &Env, image: Option<&BTreeMap<String, String>>) -> Option<Probe> {
    let Expr::Exists { read, .. } = expr else { return None };
    let info = catalog.tables.get(&read.table)?;
    let positional: Vec<_> = read.keys.iter().filter(|key| key.column.is_none()).collect();
    let mut pins = BTreeMap::new();
    if !positional.is_empty() {
        // Infer only unambiguous scalar literals/viewer positions. Raw ids
        // retain the binder’s intrinsic-id precedence and are not guessed.
        let fits = |ty: &ScalarType, expr: &Expr| match (&ty.kind, expr) {
            (TypeKind::Principal, Expr::Name { name, .. }) => name == "viewer",
            (TypeKind::Enum { variants: values }, Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Str(value), .. }) => values.contains(value),
            (TypeKind::Text { .. }, Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Str(_), .. }) => true,
            (TypeKind::Int { .. }, Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(_), .. }) => true,
            (TypeKind::Bool, Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(_), .. }) => true,
            _ => false,
        };
        let indexes: Vec<_> = info.indexes.iter().filter(|index| info.total_unique(index)
            && index.columns.len() >= positional.len()
            && index.columns.iter().zip(&positional).all(|(column,key)| info.columns.get(column).is_some_and(|ty| fits(ty, &key.value)))
            && index.columns.iter().skip(positional.len()).all(|column| read.keys.iter().any(|key| key.column.as_ref() == Some(column)))
            && read.index.as_ref().is_none_or(|name| name == &index.name)).collect();
        let [index] = indexes.as_slice() else { return None };
        for (column, key) in index.columns.iter().zip(positional) { pins.insert(column.clone(), key.value.clone()); }
    }
    for key in read.keys.iter().filter(|key| key.column.is_some()) {
        let column = key.column.as_ref()?;
        if pins.get(column).is_some_and(|old| crate::print::expression(old) != crate::print::expression(&key.value)) { return None; }
        pins.insert(column.clone(), key.value.clone());
    }
    if read.filter.is_some() || read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() { return None; }
    Some((read.table.clone(), pins.iter().map(|(column, value)| Some((column.clone(), term(value, env, image)?))).collect::<Option<_>>()?))
}
fn probe_branches(catalog: &Catalog, expr: &Expr, env: &Env) -> Option<Vec<GateBranch>> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "or" => {
            let mut a = probe_branches(catalog, left, env)?;
            a.extend(probe_branches(catalog, right, env)?);
            (a.len() <= LIMIT).then_some(a)
        }
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" => {
            let a = probe_branches(catalog, left, env)?;
            let b = probe_branches(catalog, right, env)?;
            if a.len().saturating_mul(b.len()) > LIMIT { return None; }
            Some(a.into_iter().flat_map(|a| b.iter().map(move |b| GateBranch {
                probes: a.probes.iter().chain(&b.probes).cloned().collect(),
                facts: combine(a.facts.clone(), b.facts.clone(), true),
            })).collect())
        }
        _ => Some(vec![GateBranch { probes: probe(catalog, expr, env, None).into_iter().collect(), facts: predicate(expr, env, None, true, false) }]),
    }
}
// A service equality is an independent caller alternative, never evidence for
// a human role. Inequalities, negation and mixed human ORs do not qualify.
fn service_only(expr: &Expr) -> bool {
    match expr {
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "=" => {
            let pair = |a: &Expr, b: &Expr| matches!(a, Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer")
                && matches!(b, Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Str(value), .. } if value.starts_with("service:") && value.len() > 8);
            pair(left, right) || pair(right, left)
        }
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" => service_only(left) || service_only(right),
        _ => false,
    }
}
fn gate_note(catalog: &Catalog, p: &ProgramDecl, table: &str, rule: &RuleDecl, image: &BTreeMap<String, String>, env: &Env, facts: &Facts, site: &crate::Site) -> Option<Diagnostic> {
    if !possible(facts) { return None; }
    let mut human = &rule.value;
    let mut services = Vec::new();
    fn human_arm<'a>(expr: &'a Expr, services: &mut Vec<&'a Expr>) -> &'a Expr {
        if let Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = expr && op == "or" {
            if service_only(left) { services.push(left); return human_arm(right, services); }
            if service_only(right) { services.push(right); return human_arm(left, services); }
        }
        expr
    }
    human = human_arm(human, &mut services);
    let need = probe(catalog, human, env, Some(image))?;
    let proves = |branch: &GateBranch| branch.probes.iter().any(|have| have.0 == need.0 && need.1.iter().all(|(key, value)| have.1.get(key) == Some(value)))
        || services.iter().any(|service| !possible(&combine(combine(facts.clone(), branch.facts.clone(), true), predicate(service, env, Some(image), false, true), true)));
    let viable = |branch: &&GateBranch| possible(&combine(facts.clone(), branch.facts.clone(), true));
    let (gate, _) = env.gates.iter().find(|(_, branches)| {
        let Some(branches) = branches else { return false };
        let branches: Vec<_> = branches.iter().filter(viable).collect();
        branches.iter().any(|b| proves(b)) && branches.iter().any(|b| !proves(b))
    })?;
    if env.gates.iter().any(|(_, branches)| branches.as_ref().is_some_and(|branches| {
        let branches: Vec<_> = branches.iter().filter(viable).collect();
        !branches.is_empty() && branches.iter().all(|b| proves(b))
    })) { return None; }
    Some(Diagnostic::new(site, "N_REQUIRE_REFUSED", format!("{}: mutation require `{gate}` has a caller branch that does not establish {table}'s table {effect} rule `{rule_text}` at {rule_site}; those callers may pass require and still be refused by table authority. Roles can overlap; this is a missing authority proof, not a claim that the audiences are disjoint", p.name, effect = rule.effect.word(), rule_text = crate::print::expression(&rule.value), rule_site = rule.site), "require the table's role in every admitted branch, or deliberately widen the table write rule; a mutation require never grants table authority. See: guide rule-recipes own-or-staff").guide("rule-recipes"))
}
fn term(expr: &Expr, env: &Env, row: Option<&BTreeMap<String, String>>) -> Option<String> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" => Some("viewer".into()),
        Expr::Name { name, .. } => env
            .values
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .or_else(|| env.rows.get(name)?.1.get("id").cloned()),
        Expr::Literal {
            value: Literal::Number(text),
            site,
        } => Some(format!(
            "literal:Number({})",
            super::integer_literal(text, site).ok()?
        )),
        Expr::Literal { value, .. } => Some(format!("literal:{value:?}")),
        Expr::Member { base, name, .. } => match base.as_ref() {
            Expr::Focal { .. } => row?.get(name).cloned(),
            Expr::Name { name: alias, .. } => env.rows.get(alias)?.1.get(name).cloned(),
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}
fn predicate(
    expr: &Expr,
    env: &Env,
    row: Option<&BTreeMap<String, String>>,
    positive: bool,
    table_rule: bool,
) -> Facts {
    match expr {
        Expr::Name { name, .. }
            if ["true", "false"].contains(&name.as_str())
                || table_rule && ["allow", "deny"].contains(&name.as_str()) =>
        {
            if (["allow", "true"].contains(&name.as_str())) == positive {
                unknown()
            } else {
                vec![]
            }
        }
        Expr::Literal {
            value: Literal::Bool(value),
            ..
        } => {
            if *value == positive {
                unknown()
            } else {
                vec![]
            }
        }
        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "not" => {
            predicate(value, env, row, !positive, table_rule)
        }
        Expr::Binary {
            op, left, right, ..
        } if op == "and" || op == "or" => combine(
            predicate(left, env, row, positive, table_rule),
            predicate(right, env, row, positive, table_rule),
            (op == "and") == positive,
        ),
        Expr::Binary {
            op, left, right, ..
        } if op == "=" || op == "!=" => match (term(left, env, row), term(right, env, row)) {
            (Some(a), Some(b)) => vec![vec![(a, b, (op == "=") == positive)]],
            _ => unknown(),
        },
        // Program probes are reads, whereas rule probes see hidden rows. Never
        // equate them or assume unrelated roster rows cannot overlap.
        _ => unknown(),
    }
}
fn row(
    catalog: &Catalog,
    table: &str,
    keys: &[KeyPart],
    env: &Env,
) -> Option<BTreeMap<String, String>> {
    let info = catalog.tables.get(table)?;
    let mut keys = keys.to_vec();
    if keys.iter().any(|k| k.column.is_none()) {
        let [key] = keys.as_mut_slice() else {
            return None;
        };
        let known_id = match &key.value {
            Expr::Name { name, .. } => {
                env.references.get(name).is_some_and(|t| t == table)
                    || env.rows.get(name).is_some_and(|(t, _)| t == table)
            }
            Expr::Member { base, name, .. } if name == "id" => {
                matches!(base.as_ref(), Expr::Name { name, .. } if env.rows.get(name).is_some_and(|(t, _)| t == table))
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        if !known_id {
            return None;
        }
        key.column = Some("id".into());
    }
    let mut read = ReadExpr {
        table: table.into(),
        keys,
        ..super::auth_lints::empty_read(table, &info.decl.site)
    };
    // `pins` resolves only an unambiguous real index and full unique key.
    read.range = None;
    let pins = super::auth_lints::pins(catalog, &read)?;
    let key: BTreeMap<_, _> = pins
        .iter()
        .map(|(col, expr)| Some((col.clone(), term(expr, env, None)?)))
        .collect::<Option<_>>()?;
    let index = info.indexes.iter().find(|i| {
        i.is_plain() && info.total_unique(i) && i.columns.iter().all(|c| key.contains_key(c))
    })?;
    let identity = format!(
        "{table}:{:?}",
        index
            .columns
            .iter()
            .map(|c| (c, &key[c]))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
    );
    Some(
        info.columns
            .keys()
            .map(|c| {
                (
                    c.clone(),
                    key.get(c)
                        .cloned()
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("row:{identity}:{c}")),
                )
            })
            .collect(),
    )
}
fn opaque_effect(expr: &Expr) -> bool {
    matches!(
        expr,
        Expr::Write { .. }
            | Expr::Call { .. }
            | Expr::ShapeUse { .. }
            | Expr::Shape { .. }
            | Expr::Merge(_)
    ) || matches!(expr, Expr::Object { fields, .. } if fields.iter().any(|f| f.spread))
}
fn expressions(statement: &Stmt) -> Vec<Expr> {
    let mut body = vec![statement.clone()];
    let mut result = vec![];
    super::intent_walk::statements(&mut body, &mut |e| result.push(e.clone()));
    result
}
pub(super) fn notes(catalog: &Catalog) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    let mut out = vec![];
    for p in catalog
        .documents
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|d| &d.programs)
        .filter(|p| p.kind == ProgramKind::Mutation && !p.native)
    {
        let mut env = Env::default();
        for param in &p.args {
            env.values
                .insert(param.name.clone(), format!("arg:{}", param.name));
            if let TypeKind::Ref { table } = &param.type_.kind {
                env.references.insert(param.name.clone(), table.clone());
            }
        }
        let body: Vec<_> = p.prelude.iter().chain(&p.body).cloned().collect();
        visit(catalog, p, &body, env, unknown(), &mut out);
    }
    out
}
fn visit(
    catalog: &Catalog,
    p: &ProgramDecl,
    body: &[Stmt],
    mut env: Env,
    mut facts: Facts,
    out: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
) {
    for s in body {
        match s {
            Stmt::If {
                condition,
                then_body,
                else_body,
                ..
            } => {
                // A condition helper can write before either branch. Analyze
                // just the condition, not the branch bodies, for entry effects.
                let condition_stmt = Stmt::Expr {
                    value: condition.clone(),
                    site: condition.site().clone(),
                };
                if expressions(&condition_stmt).iter().any(opaque_effect) {
                    env = Env::default();
                    facts = unknown();
                }
                visit(
                    catalog,
                    p,
                    then_body,
                    env.clone(),
                    combine(
                        facts.clone(),
                        predicate(condition, &env, None, true, false),
                        true,
                    ),
                    out,
                );
                visit(
                    catalog,
                    p,
                    else_body,
                    env.clone(),
                    combine(
                        facts.clone(),
                        predicate(condition, &env, None, false, false),
                        true,
                    ),
                    out,
                );
                // Branch writes/rebindings may invalidate every entry fact.
                env = Env::default();
                facts = unknown();
                continue;
            }
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => {
                visit(catalog, p, body, Env::default(), unknown(), out);
                env = Env::default();
                facts = unknown();
                continue;
            }
            Stmt::As { .. } => {
                env = Env::default();
                facts = unknown();
                continue;
            }
            Stmt::Break { .. } | Stmt::Continue { .. } => break,
            _ => {}
        }
        let es = expressions(s);
        // Calls and compound effects are opaque; drop stale facts before any
        // expression that could change a witnessed row, including helper calls.
        let effects = es.iter().filter(|e| opaque_effect(e)).count();
        if effects > 0
            && !(effects == 1
                && matches!(
                    s,
                    Stmt::Expr {
                        value: Expr::Write { .. },
                        ..
                    } | Stmt::Bind {
                        value: Expr::Write { .. },
                        ..
                    } | Stmt::Return {
                        value: Expr::Write { .. },
                        ..
                    }
                ))
        {
            facts = unknown();
            env = Env::default();
        }
        for e in &es {
            if let Expr::Write {
                op: op @ (WriteOp::Insert | WriteOp::Update | WriteOp::Upsert | WriteOp::Delete),
                table,
                keys,
                fields,
                site,
                ..
            } = e
            {
                let Some(info) = catalog.tables.get(table) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if info.decl.columns.iter().any(|c| c.written_by.is_some())
                    || fields.iter().any(|f| f.spread)
                {
                    continue;
                }
                let effect = match op { WriteOp::Insert => Effect::Insert, WriteOp::Delete => Effect::Delete, _ => Effect::Update };
                let Some(rule) = info.decl.rules.iter().find(|r| r.effect == effect) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let image = if matches!(op, WriteOp::Insert) {
                    info.columns.keys().map(|column| (column.clone(), format!("insert-unknown:{site}:{column}"))).collect()
                } else if let Some(image) = row(catalog, table, keys, &env) { image } else { continue };
                let mut next = image.clone();
                for field in fields {
                    let value = field.value.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| Expr::Name {
                        name: field.name.clone(),
                        site: field.site.clone(),
                    });
                    next.insert(
                        field.name.clone(),
                        term(&value, &env, None)
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("next-unknown:{}:{}", site, field.name)),
                    );
                }
                let image = if matches!(op, WriteOp::Insert) { next.clone() } else { image };
                if let Some(note) = gate_note(catalog, p, table, rule, &image, &env, &facts, site) { out.push(note); }
                let (authority, failing_image) = if let [old_alias, next_alias] = rule.bindings.as_slice() {
                    let mut images = env.clone();
                    images
                        .rows
                        .insert(old_alias.clone(), (table.clone(), image.clone()));
                    images
                        .rows
                        .insert(next_alias.clone(), (table.clone(), next));
                    (predicate(&rule.value, &images, None, true, true), "named transition (old/next)")
                } else if rule.bindings.is_empty() && matches!(op, WriteOp::Insert | WriteOp::Delete) {
                    (predicate(&rule.value, &env, Some(&image), true, true), if matches!(op, WriteOp::Insert) { "insert image" } else { "delete image" })
                } else if rule.bindings.is_empty() {
                    let old = predicate(&rule.value, &env, Some(&image), true, true);
                    let next = predicate(&rule.value, &env, Some(&next), true, true);
                    let failing_image = if !possible(&combine(facts.clone(), old.clone(), true)) { "old image" }
                        else if !possible(&combine(facts.clone(), next.clone(), true)) { "next image" }
                        else { "combined old/next images" };
                    (combine(old, next, true), failing_image)
                } else {
                    continue;
                };
                if possible(&facts)
                    && !possible(&combine(facts.clone(), authority, true))
                    && !matches!(
                        &rule.value,
                        Expr::Literal {
                            value: Literal::Bool(false),
                            ..
                        }
                    )
                    && !matches!(&rule.value, Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "deny" || name == "false")
                {
                    let arm = if matches!(
                        e,
                        Expr::Write {
                            op: WriteOp::Upsert,
                            ..
                        }
                    ) {
                        "update arm of this upsert"
                    } else {
                        effect.word()
                    };
                    let rewrite = if matches!(op, WriteOp::Insert | WriteOp::Delete) {
                        format!("amend the table {} rule or caller gate; require decides intent, not table authority; see: guide rule-recipes role-workflow", effect.word())
                    } else if rule.bindings.is_empty() {
                        format!("amend the table update rule or caller gate; require decides intent, not table authority. If the policy should judge only the pre-write state, choose `{}`; this changes authority, so keep every intended next-image constraint. see: guide rule-recipes update-images", super::rule_operator::old_update_source(&rule.value))
                    } else {
                        "amend the named table transition or caller gate; require decides intent, not table authority. see: guide rule-recipes update-images".into()
                    };
                    out.push(Diagnostic::new(site, "N_WRITE_DENIED", format!("{}: table authorization layer, {failing_image}: no caller satisfying the preceding require/branch conditions can pass {table}'s {} rule at {}; the {arm} cannot pass that rule", p.name, effect.word(), rule.site), rewrite).guide("rule-recipes"));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Stmt::Bind {
            names,
            value,
            site: _,
            ..
        } = s
        {
            if let [alias] = names.as_slice() {
                // Use the old environment for RHS evaluation before rebinding.
                let scalar = term(value, &env, None);
                let base = if let Expr::Assert { value, .. } = value {
                    value.as_ref()
                } else {
                    value
                };
                let lookup = if let Expr::Read(read) = base {
                    row(catalog, &read.table, &read.keys, &env).map(|r| (read, r))
                } else {
                    None
                };
                if let Some((read, image)) = &lookup
                    && matches!(value, Expr::Read(_))
                    && read.range.is_none()
                    && read.filter.is_none()
                    && read.index.is_none()
                {
                    let info = &catalog.tables[&read.table];
                    if info.through.is_none()
                        && info.maintained.is_none()
                        && let Some(rule) =
                            info.decl.rules.iter().find(|r| r.effect == Effect::Read)
                    {
                        let authority = predicate(&rule.value, &env, Some(image), true, true);
                        if possible(&facts) && !possible(&combine(facts.clone(), authority, true)) {
                            out.push(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "N_LOOKUP_NEVER_VISIBLE", format!("{}: this nullable {} point lookup is always null for callers satisfying the preceding require/branch conditions under the read rule at {}; an `{alias} != null` branch cannot run", p.name, read.table, rule.site), "authorize these callers to read the row, or write by key under the table rule without a preliminary lookup; guide rule-recipes, enrolment into hidden things").guide("rule-recipes"));
                        }
                    }
                }
                // Facts naming the old alias are immutable symbolic snapshots;
                // rebinding conservatively drops all facts to avoid alias reuse.
                if env.values.contains_key(alias) || env.rows.contains_key(alias) {
                    facts = unknown();
                    env.gates.clear();
                }
                env.values.remove(alias);
                env.rows.remove(alias);
                env.references.remove(alias);
                if let Some(scalar) = scalar {
                    env.values.insert(alias.clone(), scalar);
                }
                if matches!(value, Expr::Assert { .. })
                    && let Some((read, image)) = lookup
                    && !catalog.tables[&read.table]
                        .decl
                        .columns
                        .iter()
                        .any(|c| c.written_by.is_some())
                {
                    env.rows.insert(alias.clone(), (read.table.clone(), image));
                }
            } else {
                env = Env::default();
                facts = unknown();
            }
        }
        if let Stmt::Require { condition, .. } = s {
            let branches = probe_branches(catalog, condition, &env);
            env.gates.push((crate::print::expression(condition), branches));
            facts = combine(facts, predicate(condition, &env, None, true, false), true);
        }
        if effects > 0 {
            facts = unknown();
            env = Env::default();
        }
        if matches!(s, Stmt::Return { .. }) {
            break;
        }
    }
}

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — ruling 17 (a), third pass: hidden immutable fields are ignored, never compared, on update and upsert.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(&self, table: &str, patch: crate::value::Supplied, readable: bool) -> Result<crate::value::Supplied, RuntimeError> {
        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#12-wave-24-loop-repairs-dx7 — protected immutable patches never compare hidden payloads.
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
        patch.remove_fields(definition.constraints.iter().filter_map(|c|match c {
            crate::schema::Constraint::Immutable {fields} => Some(fields.iter()), _ => None,
        }).flatten().filter(|field| !readable || definition.column_reads.contains_key(*field)).cloned())
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#14 — ruling 17 (b): an author condition needs a readable target; a blind patch needs none.

        if readable { Ok(()) } else { self.refusing_clause(table, "read rule"); Err(self.no_write_target()) }
    }

/// Read access shared by store and transaction snapshots.
pub(crate) trait MetadataReader {
    fn store_identity(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn generation_value(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn release_value(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn release_native_digest(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn time_audience_clock_value(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn worker_status(&self, worker: Option<&str>) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn release_revision_value(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn schema_marker(&self, marker: SchemaMarker) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn worker_session_family(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn worker_session_revision(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn worker_family_revision(&self, family: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn deployment_environment(&self) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
    fn dev_value(&self, key: DevMetadata) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError>;
}

    Replay,
    SuppressedEffects,
    HoldSchedules,
}

    fn set_dev_value(&self, key: DevMetadata, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
    fn set_deployment_environment(&self, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
    fn set_worker_status(&self, worker: Option<&str>, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
}

    }

// @ref LLP 3000.009.001.000#9.1 — validate admission, never stored values or legacy keys.
pub(crate) fn validate_value(value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if value.contains('\0') {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
            "metadata text cannot contain U+0000".into(),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}
pub(crate) fn validate_new_key(key: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if key.contains('\0') {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
            "new metadata keys cannot contain U+0000".into(),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod test_cases {
    use super::*;

    pub fn raw_values_and_worker_fences(reader: &impl MetadataReader) {
        // The caller decides how to interpret malformed and missing values.
        assert_eq!(
            reader.generation_value().unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some("invalid")
        );
        assert_eq!(reader.release_value().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(
            reader.worker_family_revision("named").unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some("2")
        );
        assert!(!crate::identity::supervisor_current(reader, "legacy", 2).unwrap());
        assert!(!crate::identity::supervisor_current(reader, "named", 1).unwrap());
        assert!(crate::identity::supervisor_current(reader, "named", 2).unwrap());
        assert!(crate::identity::supervisor_current(reader, "manual", 99).unwrap());
    }

    pub fn missing(reader: &impl MetadataReader) {
        assert_eq!(reader.store_identity().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.generation_value().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.release_value().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.release_revision_value().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.release_native_digest().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.time_audience_clock_value().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.worker_session_family().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.worker_session_revision().unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.worker_family_revision("absent").unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.worker_status(Some("absent")).unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.worker_status(None).unwrap(), None);
        assert_eq!(reader.deployment_environment().unwrap(), None);
        for key in [
            DevMetadata::Replay,
            DevMetadata::SuppressedEffects,
            DevMetadata::HoldSchedules,
        ] {
            assert_eq!(reader.dev_value(key).unwrap(), None);
        }
        for marker in [
            SchemaMarker::LiveSumCandidates,
            SchemaMarker::MaintainedIds,
            SchemaMarker::CapCounts,
            SchemaMarker::TimePublications,
            SchemaMarker::ReadThroughShortened,
        ] {
            assert_eq!(reader.schema_marker(marker).unwrap(), None);
        }
    }

    pub fn admission(handle: &(impl MetadataReader + MetadataWriter)) {
        for value in [
            "",
            "malformed",
            "-9223372036854775808",
            "9223372036854775807",
            "é日本語",
        ] {
            handle
                .set_dev_value(DevMetadata::SuppressedEffects, value)
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                handle
                    .dev_value(DevMetadata::SuppressedEffects)
                    .unwrap()
                    .as_deref(),
                Some(value)
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(
            handle
                .set_deployment_environment("bad\0value")
                .unwrap_err()
                .code(),
            "E_INPUT"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle
                .set_dev_value(DevMetadata::Replay, "bad\0value")
                .unwrap_err()
                .code(),
            "E_INPUT"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle
                .set_worker_status(Some("new\0key"), "ready")
                .unwrap_err()
                .code(),
            "E_INPUT"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle
                .set_worker_status(None, "bad\0value")
                .unwrap_err()
                .code(),
            "E_INPUT"
        );
        assert_eq!(handle.worker_status(Some("new\0key")).unwrap(), None);
    }

    pub fn advance(
        handle: &(impl MetadataReader + MetadataWriter),
        expected: Option<&str>,
        next: &str,
    ) {
        assert_eq!(
            handle.worker_status(Some("race")).unwrap().as_deref(),
            expected
        );
        handle.set_worker_status(Some("race"), next).unwrap();
    }

    pub fn independent_families(handle: &(impl MetadataReader + MetadataWriter)) {
        handle.set_dev_value(DevMetadata::Replay, "true").unwrap();
        handle
            .set_dev_value(DevMetadata::HoldSchedules, "false")
            .unwrap();
        handle.set_deployment_environment("staging").unwrap();
        handle.set_worker_status(None, "legacy").unwrap();
        handle.set_worker_status(Some("named"), "ready").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            handle.dev_value(DevMetadata::Replay).unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some("true")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle
                .dev_value(DevMetadata::HoldSchedules)
                .unwrap()
                .as_deref(),
            Some("false")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle.deployment_environment().unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some("staging")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle.worker_status(None).unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some("legacy")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            handle.worker_status(Some("named")).unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some("ready")
        );
        assert_eq!(handle.worker_status(Some("absent")).unwrap(), None);
    }
}

//! Engine-private write addressing, conditions and disclosure.
use crate::engine::runner::{Flow, Runner};
use crate::engine::rules::rule_probes;
use crate::error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError};
use crate::ir::{Builtin, Expr, IndexKeyExpr, Input, KeyProvenance, LoopDomain, Read, Scan, Stmt, WriteCondition};
use crate::schema::{ColumnType, Constraint, Effect, Table, materialize_optional_fields};
use crate::rows::index_values;
use crate::value::Value;

// Only this resolver can certify caller-evaluated natural keys.
pub(crate) struct TargetInput(());

impl Runner<'_> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — absent and hidden-refused targets restore every logical meter field.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn target_attempt<T>(&mut self, table: &str, attempt: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        let mark = self.meter.mark();
        let capture_prepaid = std::mem::replace(&mut self.capture_prepaid, false);
        let live_prepaid=std::mem::replace(&mut self.live_prepaid,false);
        let live_heap=std::mem::take(&mut self.live_heap);
        let prepaid = std::mem::replace(&mut self.maintain_prepaid, false);
        let previous_heap = std::mem::take(&mut self.maintain_heap);
        let column_prepaid = std::mem::replace(&mut self.column_prepaid, false);
        let column_heap = std::mem::take(&mut self.column_heap);
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        let assets_prepaid = std::mem::replace(&mut self.assets_prepaid, false);
        let result = self.reserve_live(table).and_then(|_| self.reserve_columns(table)).and_then(|_|attempt(self));
        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
        { self.assets_prepaid = assets_prepaid; }
        self.capture_prepaid = capture_prepaid;
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes=self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(self.live_heap);
        self.live_heap=live_heap;
        self.live_prepaid=live_prepaid;
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(self.column_heap);
        self.column_prepaid = column_prepaid;
        self.column_heap = column_heap;
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(self.maintain_heap);
        self.maintain_heap = previous_heap;
        self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
        if matches!(&result, Err(RuntimeError::Require { code, .. }) if code == "NOT_FOUND") { self.meter.restore(mark); }
        result
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.013#11.1 — reserve authorization before target existence or expiry can select a different outcome.
    pub(super) fn reserve_write_rules(&self, table: &Table, effects: &[Effect]) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let probes = effects.iter().map(|effect| rule_probes(table.rules.for_effect(*effect))).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
        if !self.meter.room(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: MeterKind::RuleProbes, actual: self.meter.used.rule_probes.saturating_add(probes), ceiling: self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes, site: self.meter.site().into() });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — reserve resolution's static worst case before the target lookup; no ceiling is changed.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn reserve_target_resolution(&mut self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, patch: &crate::value::Supplied, upsert: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if upsert { self.reserve_capture(table)?; }
        let probes = rule_probes(&table.rules.read).saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(rule_probes(&table.rules.update).saturating_mul(1 + u64::from(table.judges_old_image())))
            .saturating_add(if upsert || table.ephemeral.is_some() { rule_probes(&table.rules.insert).saturating_mul(2) } else { 0 });
        // Covers the largest cloned row allowed by the schema, the caller's patch
        // (including ill-typed fields), and the miss arm's image/default materialization.
        // Retained maps/assets share their Arc; the merge charges only memory it copies.
        let witness = self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.read).max(self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.update))
            .max(if upsert || table.ephemeral.is_some() { self.rule_scratch(&table.rules.insert) } else { 0 });
        let copy = if crate::rows::disclosed::actual_size(table) { 0 } else { row_copy_ceiling(table).saturating_mul(2) };
        let heap = copy.saturating_add(patch.heap_bytes().saturating_mul(2))
            .max(crate::rows::disclosed::admission(table)).saturating_add(witness);
        for (kind, amount, used, ceiling) in [(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes, self.meter.used.rule_probes, self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes),
            (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap, self.meter.used.heap_bytes, self.meter.ceilings.heap_bytes),
            (MeterKind::IndexEntries, if upsert { table.sequences.len() as u64 } else { 0 }, self.meter.used.index_entries, self.meter.ceilings.index_entries)] {
            if !self.meter.room(kind, amount) { return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind, actual: used.saturating_add(amount), ceiling, site: self.meter.site().into() }); }
        }
        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The merged image and its lawful copy price (LLP 3000.015 §1), which a
    /// later engine copy of the same image charges again.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn merge_patch(&mut self, table: &str, old: &Value, patch: &crate::value::Supplied, _readable: bool) -> Result<(Value, u64), RuntimeError> {
        let public = if crate::rows::disclosed::actual_size(&self.schema.tables[table]) {
            self.authorize_image(table, old.clone())?
        } else { None };
        let mut bytes = 40_u64;
        for (key, _) in old.as_object()?.iter().filter(|(key, _)| !patch.as_object().expect("patch checked").contains_key(*key)).chain(patch.as_object()?.iter()) {
            // @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — a retained field's actual size is disclosed
            // only after both row and field read authority succeed.
            let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
            let copy = if patch.as_object()?.contains_key(key) { patch.field_copy(key) } else if let Some(row) = &public { row.scalar_heap(key) } else { definition.columns.get(key).map_or(0,column_copy_ceiling) };
            bytes = bytes.saturating_add(80 + key.len() as u64 + copy);
        }
        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
        let fields = old.as_object()?.iter().filter(|(key, _)| !patch.as_object().expect("patch checked").contains_key(*key)).chain(patch.as_object()?.iter())
            .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), value.clone())).collect::<std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _>>();
        Ok((Value::Row(fields.into()), bytes))
    }

    pub(in crate::engine) fn no_write_target(&self) -> RuntimeError {
        RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".into(), message: None }
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — item 7: an unheld write target without an absence proof queues.
    pub(in crate::engine) fn write_miss(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> RuntimeError {
        if self.device {
            self.unknown_fact(table, index, key, &self.statement_site.clone());
            if let Some(message) = &mut self.missing_fact { *message = message.replace("the row or its absence is past the acquired horizon or online only", "the write target is not held on this device; only the server can resolve it"); }
            RuntimeError::Prediction(self.missing_fact.clone().expect("missing site recorded"))
        } else { self.no_write_target() }
    }

    pub(in crate::engine) fn upsert_absence_proven(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#12-wave-24-loop-repairs-dx7 — mounted scrollable text counts; hidden descendants never manufacture evidence.
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import type { Locator, FrameLocator, Selectors } from "playwright-core";

export const renderedSelector = `sb4rendered${randomUUID().replaceAll("-", "")}`;
const registrations = new WeakMap<Selectors, Promise<void>>();
let selectorReady: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
export async function registerRenderedSelector(selectors: Selectors): Promise<void> {
  let registration = registrations.get(selectors);
  if (!registration) {
    registration = selectors.register(renderedSelector, renderedTextEngine, { contentScript: true });
    registrations.set(selectors, registration);
    selectorReady = Promise.all([selectorReady, registration]).then(() => {});
    void selectorReady.catch(() => {}); // Observations await and surface this rejection.
  }
  await registration;
}

// Playwright serializes this function into its isolated selector world. Keep it
// self-contained: no application script, global callback or injected DOM marker.
function renderedTextEngine() {
  let observedText = "";
  const parent = (node: Node): Element | null => (node as Element).assignedSlot ?? node.parentElement ?? (node.getRootNode() as ShadowRoot).host ?? null;
  function textInView(node: Node): string {
    const text = node.textContent ?? "";
    if (!text) return "";
    const clips: { box: DOMRect; x: boolean; y: boolean }[] = [];
    for (let element = parent(node); element; element = parent(element)) {
      const style = getComputedStyle(element);
      if (style.display === "none" || style.opacity === "0" || style.contentVisibility === "hidden") return "";
      const clipsOverflow = style.display !== "contents" && style.display !== "inline";
      // Scrollports can reveal mounted text without changing the proof's DOM.
      // Real clips still exclude text, including zero-sized scrollports.
      const scrollable = (overflow: string, size: number) => /^(auto|scroll)$/.test(overflow) && size > 0;
      const html = element as HTMLElement;
      const x = clipsOverflow && style.overflowX !== "visible" && !scrollable(style.overflowX, html.clientWidth);
      const y = clipsOverflow && style.overflowY !== "visible" && !scrollable(style.overflowY, html.clientHeight);
      if (x || y) {
        let box = element.getBoundingClientRect();
        const html = element as HTMLElement;
        if (typeof html.offsetWidth === "number") {
          const scaleX = html.offsetWidth ? box.width / html.offsetWidth : 1;
          const scaleY = html.offsetHeight ? box.height / html.offsetHeight : 1;
          box = new DOMRect(box.left + html.clientLeft * scaleX, box.top + html.clientTop * scaleY, html.clientWidth * scaleX, html.clientHeight * scaleY);
        }
        clips.push({ box, x, y });
      }
    }
    const visible = (rect: DOMRect) => {
      let left = rect.left, right = rect.right, top = rect.top, bottom = rect.bottom;
      for (const {box,x,y} of clips) {
        if (x) { left = Math.max(left,box.left); right = Math.min(right,box.right); }
        if (y) { top = Math.max(top,box.top); bottom = Math.min(bottom,box.bottom); }
      }
      return right > left && bottom > top;
    };
    const range = document.createRange(); range.selectNodeContents(node);
    const rects = [...range.getClientRects()];
    if (!rects.some(visible)) return "";
    if (rects.every(rect => clips.every(({box,x,y}) => (!x || rect.left >= box.left && rect.right <= box.right) && (!y || rect.top >= box.top && rect.bottom <= box.bottom)))) return text;
    // A clipped prefix must not claim the hidden suffix. Range geometry also
    // works through display:contents and wrappers with visible overflow.
    let result = "", offset = 0;
    for (const character of text) {
      range.setStart(node,offset); offset += character.length; range.setEnd(node,offset);
      if ([...range.getClientRects()].some(visible)) result += character;
    }
    return result;
  }
  function queryAll(root: Document | Element | ShadowRoot, selector: string): Element[] {
    const options = JSON.parse(selector) as { source: string; flags: string; regex: boolean; exact: boolean };
    const regex = options.regex ? new RegExp(options.source, options.flags) : null;
    const needle = options.source.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    const found: Element[] = [];
    const matches = (text: string) => {
      if (!text) return false;
      if (regex) { regex.lastIndex = 0; return regex.test(text); }
      return options.exact ? text === needle : text.toLowerCase().includes(needle.toLowerCase());
    };
    const walk = (node: Node, ancestorSuppressed = false): { text: string; matched: boolean } => {
      if (node.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE) return { text: ancestorSuppressed ? "" : textInView(node), matched: false };
      if (node.nodeType !== Node.ELEMENT_NODE && node.nodeType !== Node.DOCUMENT_NODE && node.nodeType !== Node.DOCUMENT_FRAGMENT_NODE) return { text: "", matched: false };
      const element = node.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE ? node as HTMLElement : null;
      if (element && (/^(INPUT|TEXTAREA|SCRIPT|STYLE|NOSCRIPT|TEMPLATE)$/.test(element.tagName) || element.isContentEditable)) return { text: "", matched: false };
      const style = element ? getComputedStyle(element) : null;
      if (style?.display === "none" || style?.opacity === "0") return { text: "", matched: false };
      const suppressed = style ? style.visibility === "hidden" || style.visibility === "collapse" : ancestorSuppressed;
      const nodes = element?.shadowRoot ? element.shadowRoot.childNodes
        : element?.tagName === "SLOT" ? ((element as HTMLSlotElement).assignedNodes({flatten:true}).length ? (element as HTMLSlotElement).assignedNodes({flatten:true}) : element.childNodes) : node.childNodes;
      let text = "", descendantMatch = false;
      for (const child of nodes) {
        const result = walk(child, suppressed);
        // Block boundaries are whitespace, never concatenated words from
        // unrelated paragraph siblings. Inline RN spans retain their text.
        const block = child.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE && /^(block|flex|grid|table|list-item)/.test(getComputedStyle(child as Element).display);
        text += block ? ` ${result.text} ` : result.text;
        descendantMatch ||= result.matched;
      }
      const normalized = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
      const box = element?.getBoundingClientRect();
      const visible = element && !suppressed && box && box.width > 0 && box.height > 0;
      const ownMatch = !!visible && !/^(HTML|BODY)$/.test(element.tagName) && matches(normalized);
      if (ownMatch && !descendantMatch) found.push(element);
      return { text, matched: ownMatch || descendantMatch };
    };
    observedText = walk(root).text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    return found;
  }
  return { queryAll, query: (root: Document | Element | ShadowRoot, selector: string) => queryAll(root, selector)[0] ?? null,
    text: (root: Element) => { queryAll(root, '{"source":"","flags":"","regex":false,"exact":true}'); return observedText; } };
}

export function visibleText(locator: Locator, timeout: number): Promise<string> {
  // Build the function in Node, then let Playwright serialize it. Passing an
  // arrow as a string would evaluate to the function rather than invoke it.
  const reader = new Function("element", `return (${renderedTextEngine.toString()})().text(element);`) as (element: Element) => string;
  return locator.evaluate(reader, undefined, { timeout });
}

// Optional peer: CLI/process helpers still import and run when it is absent.
// Keep this graph synchronously require-able. Registration starts during import;
// withBrowser awaits that same promise before creating its context. Caller-owned
// browsers finish asynchronous launch before running a selector.
try { void registerRenderedSelector(createRequire(import.meta.url)("playwright-core").selectors).catch(() => {}); }
catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND" && (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "MODULE_NOT_FOUND") throw error; }

// Locator construction stays synchronous for CommonJS callers. Actions wait
// for optional-peer selector registration, including when the page predates
// the proof import. Preserve synchronous Locator/FrameLocator chaining.
const locatorWrappers = new WeakMap<object, object>();
const locatorChains = new Set(["locator", "filter", "describe", "first", "last", "nth", "and", "or", "frameLocator", "contentFrame", "owner"]);
export function registeredLocator<T extends Locator | FrameLocator>(locator: T): T {
  const known = locatorWrappers.get(locator);
  if (known) return known as T;
  const wrapped = new Proxy(locator, {
    get(target, key) {
      const value = Reflect.get(target, key, target);
      if (typeof value !== "function" || key === "constructor") return value;
      if (typeof key !== "string" || key === "page" || key === "toString" || key === "_inspect" || key === "_equals") return value.bind(target);
      if (locatorChains.has(key) || key.startsWith("getBy")) return (...args: unknown[]) => registeredLocator(Reflect.apply(value, target, args));
      return (...args: unknown[]) => selectorReady.then(() => Reflect.apply(value, target, args));
    },
  });
  locatorWrappers.set(locator, wrapped); locatorWrappers.set(wrapped, wrapped);
  return wrapped;
}

        },
    }
}
