//! Field writes use the old owner; row transition rules still constrain them.
// @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — ownership grants only the explicitly touched owned fields.
use super::runner::Runner;
use super::rules::{self, Probe};
use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, schema::{Effect, RuleExpr}, value::Value};

/// Delivery accounting must not make another recipient's unknown membership
/// a dependency of the writer's prediction. Server witnesses remain exact.
struct DeliveryProbe<'a, 'b> {
    runner: &'a mut Runner<'b>,
    known: bool,
    allowance: &'a super::Authorization,
}

impl Probe for DeliveryProbe<'_, '_> {
    fn take_changes(&mut self) -> Option<Vec<(i64, super::rules::Verdict)>> { self.runner.witness_changes.take() }
    fn replace_expiry(&mut self, expiry: Option<i64>) -> Option<i64> { self.runner.next_expiry.replace(expiry) }
    fn exists(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value], equalities: &[(String, Value)]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.runner.read_charge(MeterKind::RuleProbes, 1)? { return Ok(false); }
        let (present, known) = self.runner.probe_witness(self.allowance, table, index, key, equalities, false)?;
        self.known &= known;
        Ok(present)
    }

    fn created(&mut self, _table: &str, _index: &str, _key: &[Value]) -> bool { false }
}

impl<'r> Runner<'r> {
    pub(crate) fn field_owner_can_read(&mut self, rule: &RuleExpr, owner: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        // Recipient witnesses are exact but are not the caller's observations.
        // Partition accounting prepays their schema-derived probe/step bound.
        // A recipient's witness deadline never enters the writer's answer: the scope is dropped, not emitted.
        let delivery_expiry = self.next_expiry.scope();
        let result = self.authorized_scratch(self.rule_scratch(rule), &[], |runner, allowance| {
            let mut probe = DeliveryProbe { runner, known: true, allowance };
            let readable = rules::evaluate(rule, owner, None, row, false, &mut probe)?;
            Ok(readable && probe.known)
        });
        drop(delivery_expiry);
        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn prepay_field_delivery(&mut self, rule: &RuleExpr, slots: u64, maintained: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let probes = slots.saturating_mul(rules::rule_probes(rule));
        if maintained {
            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes)?;
            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, slots)?;
        } else {
            self.meter.charge(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes)?;
            self.meter.step(slots)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(super) fn authorize_fields(&self, table: &str, row: &Value, supplied: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
        let fields = supplied.as_object()?;
        let mut owned = false;
        let mut ordinary = false;
        for field in fields.keys().filter(|field| field.as_str() != "id") {
            if let Some(authority) = definition.written_by.get(field) {
                owned = true;
                if !self.context.is_system() && row.field(&authority.owner).ok() != Some(&Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone())) {
                    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
                    self.refusing_clause(table, &format!("field authority {field}"));
                    return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_FIELD_AUTHORITY", message: format!("{table}.{field} is written by .{}; omit {field} or write as the principal in .{} (guide rules)", authority.owner, authority.owner) });
                }
            } else { ordinary = true; }
        }
        Ok(owned && !ordinary)
    }

    pub(super) fn authorize_update_fields(&mut self, table: &str, old: &Value, next: &Value, patch: &Value, readable: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let owned_only = self.authorize_fields(table, old, patch).map_err(|error| if readable { error } else { self.no_write_target() })?;
        // An unrelated owner's omitted field is unknown, not its literal
        // default. It prevents prediction only when this transition needs it,
        // or when changing ownership would expose it to this device.
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
        if self.device && (definition.column_server_reads() || definition.column_reads.keys().any(|field|
            patch.as_object().is_ok_and(|p| !p.contains_key(field))
            && !definition.local_column_readable(field,old,Some(&self.context.viewer)) && definition.local_column_readable(field,next,Some(&self.context.viewer)))) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("{table}: this transition must acquire a protected cell; queue it for the server (guide rules)")));
        }
        if self.device && definition.written_by.iter().any(|(field, authority)|
            !authority.audience && old.field(&authority.owner).ok() != Some(&Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone()))
            && ((!owned_only || definition.update_transition) && definition.rules.update.needs_field_value(field, &definition.columns[field])
                || next.field(&authority.owner).ok() == Some(&Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone())))) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("{table}: this transition needs another principal's private field; queue it for the server (guide rules)")));
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — a named transition is not permission to test guesses against someone else's private value.
        if !self.context.is_system() && let Some((field, authority)) = definition.written_by.iter().find(|(field, authority)|
            !authority.audience && old.field(&authority.owner).ok() != Some(&Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone()))
            && definition.rules.update.needs_field_value(field, &definition.columns[*field])) {
            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
            self.refusing_clause(table, &format!("field authority {field}"));
            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_FIELD_AUTHORITY", message: format!("{table}.{field}: this transition needs the private value written by .{}; write as that owner or declare readable by audience (guide rules)", authority.owner) } } else { self.no_write_target() });
        }
        let transition = self.schema.tables[table].update_transition;
        if (!owned_only || transition) && !self.check_rule(table, Effect::Update, Some(old), next)? {
            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Rule { table: table.into(), effect: Effect::Update } } else { self.no_write_target() });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) fn column_readable(&mut self, definition: &crate::schema::Table, field: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if self.context.is_system() { return Ok(true); }
        let Some(rule) = definition.column_reads.get(field) else { return Ok(true); };
        self.rule_dependencies(rule);
        if self.device && !rule.column_row_local() { return Ok(false); }
        let viewer=self.context.viewer.clone();
        self.authorized_scratch(self.rule_scratch(rule), &[(MeterKind::RuleProbes,rules::rule_probes(rule))], |runner, allowance| {
            let mut probe=super::read::RuleProbe { runner, allowance };
            rules::evaluate(rule,&viewer,None,&crate::schema::row_image(row,definition),false,&mut probe)
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn disclosed_row<'a>(&mut self, definition: &'a crate::schema::Table, row: Value) -> Result<crate::value::Disclosed<'a>,RuntimeError> {
        if let Some(system)=self.system_access() { return Ok(definition.system_fields(row,&system)); }
        let mut grants=std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        for field in definition.column_reads.keys() {
            if self.column_readable(definition,field,&row)? { grants.insert(field.clone()); }
        }
        Ok(definition.project_fields(row,Some(&self.context.viewer)).with_column_grants(grants))
    }

    pub(crate) fn project_row_if_readable(&mut self, table: &str, row: Value) -> Result<Option<super::authorized_point::AuthorizedRow<'r>>, RuntimeError> {
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
        // A merge may retain previously authorized results after its next lane
        // cuts. Revalidate their authority internally without treating that
        // existing logical cut as a denied row. Preserve the original cut.
        let cap = self.meter.capped_at.take();
        let result = self.authorized_scratch(self.rule_scratch(&definition.rules.read), &[], |runner, _| runner.authorize_image(table,row));
        if cap.is_some() { self.meter.capped_at = cap; }
        result
    }

    pub(crate) fn project_row(&mut self, table: &str, row: Value) -> Result<super::authorized_point::AuthorizedRow<'r>, RuntimeError> {
        self.project_row_if_readable(table, row)?.ok_or_else(|| { self.refusing_clause(table, "read rule"); self.no_write_target() })
    }

    pub(super) fn private_scan_authority(&self, table: &str, uniform: bool, admitted: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        // A bounded hidden-row walk exposes population through both its meter
        // and its cut. Require a readable scope before walking protected rows.
        if !uniform && !admitted && self.schema.tables[table].written_by.values().any(|a| !a.audience) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_FIELD_AUTHORITY", message: format!("{table}: scope this read to a uniformly readable audience before scanning rows with private fields (guide rules)") });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

use crate::ast::Document;

pub use program::BoundProgram;
pub use aggregate_copies::truth as rule_truth;
use snapback4_core::schema::Schema;

pub struct Bound {
    pub invariants: Vec<security::Invariant>,
    /// Receipt member operation names, needed only by TypeScript emission.
    pub receipt_members: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// Compiler-side source map; never serialized into the client backend.
    pub refusal_sites: std::collections::BTreeMap<(String, String), String>,
    pub view_types: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, crate::types::Ty>,
    /// Authoring-only opt-in; never stored in the core schema, IR or wire.
    pub server: bool,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub programs: Vec<BoundProgram>,
    pub personas: Vec<String>,
    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    /// Facts the compiler can state that are not errors: a page that is
    /// never `complete` because its read rule is not decided by its prefix.
    pub notes: Vec<Diagnostic>,
}

pub fn bind(documents: Vec<Document>) -> Bound {
    let mut bound = bind_unverified(documents.clone());
    crate::repair::verify_bound(&documents, &mut bound.diagnostics);
    bound
}

// Repair checks run the same planner and admission, without recursively
// verifying the diagnostics from a rejected candidate.
pub(crate) fn bind_unverified(mut documents: Vec<Document>) -> Bound {
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    operation_evolution::expand(&mut documents, &mut diagnostics);
    let mut first_identity = None;
    for document in &documents {
        if let (Some(methods), Some(site)) = (document.identity, document.identity_site.as_ref()) {
            if let Some((first_methods, first_site)) = &first_identity {
                diagnostics.push(crate::parser::repeated_identity(
                    site,
                    *first_methods,
                    first_site,
                    methods,
                ));
            } else {
                first_identity = Some((methods, site.clone()));
            }
        }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — catalog provenance comes from source, before any generated declarations.
    let authored_indexes = documents.iter().flat_map(|doc|
        doc.tables.iter().map(|t| (&t.name, &t.indexes))
            .chain(doc.maintains.iter().map(|m| (&m.name, &m.indexes))))
        .map(|(name, indexes)| (name.clone(), indexes.iter().map(|i| i.name.clone()).collect())).collect();
    receipts::expand(&mut documents, &mut diagnostics);
    ephemeral::declarations(&documents, &mut diagnostics);
    helper_names::normalize(&mut documents, &mut diagnostics);
    let server = documents.iter().any(|doc| doc.server);
    server::admit(&mut documents, &mut diagnostics);
    let feeds = feed_view::expand(&mut documents, &mut diagnostics);
    // Following expansion adds its durable timeline inputs. Recheck before lowering.
    if !feeds.is_empty() { ephemeral::declarations(&documents, &mut diagnostics); }
    let documents = timeline::expand(documents, &mut diagnostics);
    let personas: Vec<String> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.personas.iter().cloned()).collect();
    let mut catalog = Catalog::build(documents, &mut diagnostics);
    catalog.feed_views = feeds;
    page_shapes::hoist(&mut catalog);
    mixed_keys::normalize(&mut catalog);
    intent::table_order(&mut catalog);
    intent_aggregates::remember_domains(&mut catalog);
    intent_search::capture(&mut catalog);
    intent_variants::expand(&mut catalog);
    intent_views::expand(&mut catalog, &mut diagnostics);
    // After argument-presence variants: `x = null or …` stays theirs (cursor validation across variants).
    where_guards::lower(&mut catalog);
    let stable_fields = catalog.tables.iter().map(|(name, table)| {
        let mut fields: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = table.decl.columns.iter()
            .filter(|column| column.written_by.is_none() && column.maintained.is_none()).map(|column| column.name.clone()).collect();
        fields.insert("id".into()); (name.clone(), fields)
    }).collect();
    for doc in &mut catalog.documents { for program in &mut doc.programs { stable_page_keys::lower_program(program, &stable_fields); } }
    intent::plan(&mut catalog, &mut diagnostics);
    reference_actions::indexes(&mut catalog);
    let mut schema = schema::bind_schema(&catalog, &mut diagnostics);
    schema.authored_indexes = snapback4_core::schema::inspection::AuthoredIndexes(Some(authored_indexes));
    timeline::admit(&catalog, &mut schema, &mut diagnostics);
    backfills::bind(&catalog, &mut schema, &mut diagnostics);
    delivery::bind(&catalog, &mut schema, &mut diagnostics);
    receipts::bind(&catalog, &mut schema, &mut diagnostics);
    schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
    reference_actions::bind(&catalog, &mut schema, &mut diagnostics);
    // @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — timeline mappings exist only after lowering both spellings.
    for issue in snapback4_core::schema::field_authority::validate(&schema) {
        if !diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_FIELD_AUTHORITY" && d.message == issue.message) {
            diagnostics.push(crate::diag::Diagnostic::new(&catalog.site_for(&issue.path), "E_FIELD_AUTHORITY", issue.message,
                "declare readable by audience before using a private field in a timeline mapping or predicate").guide("rules"));
        }
    }
    // Timeline ownership is resolved after the ordinary schema checks.
    for issue in snapback4_core::schema::columns::timeline_issues(&schema) {
        diagnostics.push(columns::refusal(&catalog.site_for(&issue.path), issue.message));
    }
    key_bound::check(&catalog, &schema, &mut diagnostics);
    let mut view_types: std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _> = catalog.feed_views.iter().map(|(name, plan)| (name.clone(), plan.ty())).collect();
    for doc in &catalog.documents {
        for decl in doc.programs.iter().filter(|decl| decl.name.starts_with("$view:")) {
            if let Some(bound) = program::Binder::bind(&catalog, &schema, "schema", decl, &mut diagnostics) {
                view_types.extend(bound.view_types);
            }
        }
    }
    catalog.view_types = view_types.clone();
    for doc in &mut catalog.documents { doc.programs.retain(|decl| !decl.name.starts_with("$view:")); }
    let mut programs = Vec::new();
    let mut names = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    let mut api_roots = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();

//! Recover a version, not invented compiler facts, from an older app.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000#6-upgrade-evidence — direct-install Exact rebuild guidance shares history acknowledgment.
use super::*;
use std::fs;
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#11-wave-11-runtime-upgrade-history — history acknowledgment is independent of compiler qualification.

fn exact(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    snapback4_lang::release_changes::version(text).map(|_| text.to_owned())
}
fn json_version(text: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let value: Json = serde_json::from_str(text).ok()?;
    exact(value[key].as_str()?)
}
pub(super) fn locked_version(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if let Ok(lock) = serde_json::from_str::<Json>(text) {
        if let Some(version) = lock.pointer("/packages/node_modules~1snapback4/version").or_else(|| lock.pointer("/dependencies/snapback4/version")).and_then(Json::as_str).and_then(exact) { return Some(version); }
    }
    // Bun's JSONC package tuple; pnpm's importer resolution (not specifier).
    let mut versions = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    for (position, _) in text.match_indices("snapback4@") {
        let tail = &text[position + "snapback4@".len()..];
        let candidate = tail.split(|c: char| !(c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-'))).next().unwrap_or("");
        if let Some(version) = exact(candidate) { versions.insert(version); }
    }
    let lines: Vec<_> = text.lines().collect();
    for (index, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
        if line.trim().trim_matches('\'').trim_matches('"') == "snapback4:" {
            for line in lines.iter().skip(index + 1).take(4) {
                if let Some(value) = line.trim().strip_prefix("version:") {
                    let value = value.trim().trim_matches(['\'', '"']).split('(').next().unwrap_or("");
                    if let Some(version) = exact(value) { versions.insert(version); }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    (versions.len() == 1).then(|| versions.into_iter().next()).flatten()
}
pub(super) fn previous(project: &Project) -> Option<String> {
    let read_version = |path, key| fs::read_to_string(path).ok().and_then(|text| json_version(&text, key));
    if let Some(version) = read_version(project.data_dir().join("runtime-version.json"), "version") { return Some(version); }
    if let Some(version) = read_version(project.data_dir().join("check-surface.json"), "version") { return Some(version); }
    if let Some(version) = read_version(project.data_dir().join("upgrade-version.json"), "version") { return Some(version); }
    if let Some(version) = read_version(project.generated_dir().join("package.json"), "snapback4Version") { return Some(version); }
    if let Some(version) = read_version(project.generated_dir().join("package.json"), "version") { return Some(version); }
    for name in ["package-lock.json", "npm-shrinkwrap.json", "bun.lock", "pnpm-lock.yaml"] {
        if let Some(version) = fs::read_to_string(project.root.join(name)).ok().and_then(|text| locked_version(&text)) { return Some(version); }
    }
    None
}
pub(super) fn report(project: &Project, json: bool) {
    if std::env::var("SNAPBACK4_UPGRADE_BASELINE").as_deref() == Ok("1") { return; }
    if let Some(previous) = previous(project) {
        let text = snapback4_lang::release_changes::interval(&previous, env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
        if !text.is_empty() { if json { eprint!("{text}"); } else { print!("{text}"); } }
        // History acknowledgment covers direct package-manager installs too,
        // even if the device preflight or schema compilation will refuse.
        if previous != env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") && !crate::exact_device::inspect(&project.root, &snapback4_core::Schema::default()).is_empty() {
            let hint = "Exact device: bun exact.mjs snapback --rebuild";
            if json { eprintln!("{hint}"); } else { println!("{hint}"); }
        }
    }
    let save = || -> std::io::Result<()> {
        fs::create_dir_all(project.data_dir())?;
        let path = project.data_dir().join("runtime-version.json");
        let temporary = path.with_extension(format!("{}.tmp", std::process::id()));
        fs::write(&temporary, serde_json::to_vec(&json!({ "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") }))?)?;
        fs::rename(temporary, path)
    };
    if let Err(error) = save() { eprintln!("check: runtime history acknowledgment not saved: {error}"); }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn lock_resolution_uses_versions_not_dependency_ranges() {
        for text in [r#"{"packages":{"node_modules/snapback4":{"version":"0.4.25"}}}"#, r#"{"dependencies":{"snapback4":{"version":"0.4.25"}}}"#, "{\n\"snapback4\": [\"snapback4@0.4.25\", \"\", {}, \"sha\"],\n}", "importers:\n  .:\n    dependencies:\n      snapback4:\n        specifier: ^0.4.24\n        version: 0.4.25", "packages:\n  snapback4@0.4.25:\n    resolution: {}"] {
            assert_eq!(locked_version(text).as_deref(), Some("0.4.25"), "{text}");
        }
        for text in ["snapback4@latest", "snapback4@0.4.24\nsnapback4@0.4.25", "snapback4:\n  specifier: ^0.4.25", "snapback4@0.4.25.1", "importers:\n  one:\n    snapback4:\n      version: 0.4.25\n  two:\n    snapback4:\n      version: 0.4.27"] { assert!(locked_version(text).is_none(), "{text}"); }
    }
}

### Per-column transformed views

A receipt records a `retained_outputs` set independently of its declaration's
active flag. When leaving a declaration, candidate-visible transformed outputs
reverse to their preimages. Outputs absent from the candidate remain transformed
in dormant storage; their set membership survives until reversal or re-entry.
Even an inactive declaration reverses those suspended fields when a later plain
schema exposes them. Whole-table suspension keeps the transformed view intact.

Re-entry preserves the saved preimage for each still-transformed output. A
fully reversed output instead captures its actual assembled source value,
including restored dormant cells and interpreted predecessor defaults, before
applying the patch. Input history and rollback preimages are separate: an input
may retain its original omitted/null interpretation while the latest rollback
view has a literal default. Ordinary writes do not erase omission provenance
when they edit a transformed output from that same original cohort.

An inverse restoring genuine absence records a transaction-local source mask.
Later evaluation cannot fill that absence from the suspended result or a default
belonging to the output schema. The mask is dropped on every exit. Earlier
recorded cohorts' staged patches are replayed into later recorded source views;
fresh declarations still share the untouched predecessor snapshot and cannot
read each other's newly staged outputs. Every decode remains heap-admitted.

Reference arguments copy any matching ordinary cell-lifetime bindings before
restoration consumes that ledger, including transformed reference cells absent
from an archived whole-row definition. Unchanged saved inputs retain existing
private bindings; inferred current bindings cannot overwrite their invalidation.

`release-backfills-v3`. Published 0.4.33's store format 3 upgrades on first use.
Unpublished experimental formats 4/5 and the older capabilities cannot silently read
this evidence layout. Package versions are not changed in this workstream.

## 4. Staging clock

Wave-20 reporting amendment: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 changes the proof
advance return to `{now, fired, held}` and explains persisted boundary holds;
operator authority and clock execution semantics below are unchanged.

Only a store durably classified staging by deploy --staging may serve with
--clock-offset. Missing/unknown classification is production. This setting
is process-local, with the same signed-duration parser and monotone elapsed
clock as dev. No serve-time mechanism can reclassify an existing production store. Restart drops the offset unless explicitly
provided again; persisted timed-disclosure floors never retreat below their captured value.

Staging exposes the existing /dev/clock/status and /dev/clock/advance only
with any full service session: these are trusted operator credentials, as for
system jobs. Production refuses even with a service token, and an explicit
production serve offset refuses with E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY before listener startup. Account, guest, read-only and unauthenticated
requests refuse. Recheck classification and session under the engine writer
before advancing. All fixture, reset, persona and dev-job doors remain closed.
Use the same advance implementation, schedule drain and ambiguous-reply law
as dev. CLI clock advance --release DIR mints its local service authority.
startServe accepts clockOffset and exposes now()/advance() through that
operator authority; it never changes store classification. Each helper control
mints a current staging-time operator session rather than caching a credential
across arbitrary time jumps. Ordinary user sessions retain normal expiry.

Hot release activation samples `shared.now()` under its engine writer, including
the persisted disclosure floor, and passes that one time through the core's
explicit `adopt_release_at`. A live preview probes the existing filesystem owner lock independently of
HTTP bind/address hints and acquires a stopped-store lock before taking its
SQLite snapshot, retaining that lock through inspection. A rollback preview
reuses its caller's existing ownership rather than probing its own lock as a

// H9 controls can load the unchanged 0.4.29 proof/witness modules via KIT2_BASELINE_DIST.
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { chromiumExecutable } from '../../../witness/lib.mjs';
const dist = process.env.KIT2_BASELINE_DIST ?? resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../dist');
const kit = await import(pathToFileURL(join(dist, 'proof.js')));
const witnessSource = readFileSync(join(dist, 'witness-web.js'), 'utf8');
async function browser(t, run) {
  const cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'kit2-contract-'));
  t.after(() => rmSync(cwd, {recursive:true,force:true}));
  await kit.withBrowser({cwd, executablePath:process.env.CHROME ?? chromiumExecutable()}, async context => run(await context.newPage(), cwd));
}
test('H9 renderedText opts into substring matching for a row with more than the needle', {timeout:30000}, async t => browser(t, async page => {
  await page.setContent('<section aria-label="Rows"><p>Proof needle — more row text</p><input value="Proof needle"></section>');
  const within = page.getByRole('region', {name:'Rows'});
  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page, 'Proof needle', {within}).count(), 0, 'exact by default');
  await assert.rejects(kit.waitForFresh(kit.renderedText(page, 'Proof needle', {within}), null, 50), /a substring match exists; pass a RegExp or `exact: false`/);
  const row = kit.renderedText(page, 'Proof needle', {within, exact:false});
  assert.equal(await row.count(), 1, 'explicit substring matches the whole rendered row');
  assert.equal(await kit.waitForFresh(row, null, {timeoutMs:500}), 'Proof needle — more row text');
  assert.equal(await kit.waitForFresh(kit.renderedText(page, /Proof needle/, {within}), null, 500), 'Proof needle — more row text');
  await assert.rejects(kit.waitForFresh(row, 'Proof needle — more row text', {timeoutMs:1000}), /locator.*last count=1.*Proof needle.*present but unchanged/);
  await assert.rejects(kit.waitForFresh(kit.renderedText(page,'missing'), null, {timeoutMs:1000}), /last count=0.*text=null.*absent/);
}));
test('DX6 composed RN text and wrapping labels preserve scope, exactness and ambiguity', {timeout:30000}, async t => browser(t, async page => {
  await page.setContent(`<section aria-label="Rows"><div><span>Order </span><span>42</span><span> saved</span></div>
    <label><span>Due </span><strong>tomorrow</strong><input value="secret value"></label>
    <p hidden>Order 42 saved</p><p>Order 42 saved later</p></section>`);
  const within = page.getByRole('region', {name:'Rows'});
  for (const text of ['Order 42 saved', /^Order 42 saved$/]) {
    const found = kit.renderedText(page, text, {within});
    assert.equal(await found.count(), 1, 'composed text selects the smallest rendered container');
    assert.equal(await kit.waitForFresh(found, null, 500), 'Order 42 saved');
  }
  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page, 'Due tomorrow', {within}).count(), 1, 'wrapping input label composes descendants without its value');
  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page,'Due tomorrow',{within:page.locator('label')}).count(),1,'a wrapping label can itself be the scope, as with Playwright getByText');
  assert.equal(await kit.statusText(page, 'Due tomorrow').count(), 1);
  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page, 'secret value', {within}).count(), 0);
  await page.getByRole('region',{name:'Rows'}).evaluate(el=>el.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', `<style>.invisible{display:none}</style><div><span hidden>Approved</span><button>Save</button></div><div><span class="invisible">Accepted</span><button>Submit</button></div><div><span style="visibility:hidden">Confirmed</span><button>Go</button></div><div><span style="opacity:0">Done</span><button>Finish</button></div><div contenteditable="true">Editable</div><div><span>Visible </span><span hidden>secret </span><strong>composed</strong></div>`));
  for(const text of ['Approved','Accepted','Confirmed','Done','Editable']) for(const needle of [text,new RegExp(text)]) assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page,needle,{within}).count(),0,`${text}: hidden or editable text is not evidence`);
  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page,'Visible composed',{within}).count(),1,'hidden adornment does not prevent composed visible evidence');
  await page.getByRole('region',{name:'Rows'}).evaluate(el=>el.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', `<div><span style="display:block;width:0;height:0;overflow:hidden">Submitted</span><button>Continue</button></div><div><span style="display:block;width:0;height:0;overflow:scroll">Finished</span></div><div><span style="display:block;width:0;height:0;border:100px solid transparent;overflow:hidden">Authorized</span></div><div style="width:10px;overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap;font:20px monospace">Completed</div><p><span style="display:contents;overflow:hidden">Layoutless </span><span style="display:inline-block;width:0;height:0;overflow:visible">wrapper</span></p>`));
  for(const text of ['Submitted','Finished','Completed','Authorized']) assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page,text,{within}).count(),0,`${text}: clipped text cannot manufacture full rendered evidence`);
  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page,'Layoutless wrapper',{within}).count(),1,'layoutless and zero-size visible-overflow wrappers retain rendered text');
  const clipped=within.locator('div').filter({has:page.locator('span').filter({hasText:'Submitted'})}).first();
  assert.equal(await kit.waitForFresh(clipped,null,500),'Continue','arbitrary locator freshness uses the same clipping rules');
  const visible=kit.renderedText(page,'Visible composed',{within});
  assert.equal(await kit.waitForFresh(visible,null,500),'Visible composed');
  await visible.evaluate(el=>el.querySelector('[hidden]').textContent='changed invisible text');
  await assert.rejects(kit.waitForFresh(visible,'Visible composed',50),/present but unchanged/);
  await assert.rejects(kit.waitForFresh(visible.filter({visible:true}),'Visible composed',50),/present but unchanged/);


  assert.equal(await kit.renderedText(page, 'order 42 saved', {within}).count(), 0, 'exact remains case sensitive');

    15	had no single recipe. This amendment supplies that recipe using the existing

    17	SEC owns self-promotion lints and security invariants; KIT4 owns unrelated

    19	
    20	`deploy <dir> --staging` classifies a **new deployment store**, under its
    21	exclusive owner, with durable metadata `deployment_environment=staging`.
    22	An existing store with no classification is production, including legacy stores;
    23	it cannot be relabelled. A staging store remains staging through deploy,
    24	rollback, restart, copying and source edits. There is no promote/relabel flag:
    25	production requires a separate fresh deployment without --staging and real
    26	operator provisioning. --check never creates the classification. Repeating
    27	--staging on an already staging store is allowed, including while serve runs;
    28	it verifies the existing classification without changing it. Malicious edits by
    29	the filesystem/database owner are outside the threat model, as for service tokens.
    30	This is a deployment-lifetime boundary stronger than a mutable per-release flag:
    31	production source or a seed plan cannot opt a production store into test setup.

    33	## 2. Real staging accounts
    34	
    35	`GET /auth/config` reports `development` independently of door availability,
    36	`devDoors`, and `environment` (`development`, `staging`, or `production`).
    37	Missing/unknown environment metadata is production. serve remains bearer-only
    38	in both environments, with the same password verifiers, session lifetimes,
    39	rules, rate limits, clock and data plane. No password hashing or grant bypass.
    40	
    41	`startServe(dir, options)` additionally returns `operatorToken(service =
    42	"operator", days = 1)` and `seedAccounts(options)`. Minting uses the existing
    43	local CLI proof protocol, captures secret stdout in memory and never writes
    44	tokens into proof logs. It confers only that service seat's existing authority.
    45	Tokens may also be requested on production for first-admin setup.
    46

    48	role, then calls the declared mutation as service:operator; `args(account)`
    49	maps the account to application arguments (default `{principal, role}`).
    50	`provision` is a generated mutation handle or `{name}`, including qualified names such as `accounts.provision`. The returned records
    51	contain email, password, principal, token and expiresAt, grouped by role.
    52	`startServe(dir, {seedUsers: options})` performs the same setup before returning
    53	and exposes those records as `sessions`. Before minting or creating accounts,
    54	the helper requires environment=staging and development=false. Production,
    55	legacy and dev hosts refuse. Inputs are validated before effects; signup is
    56	sequential, bounded, respects identity throttling, and never retries an ambiguous
    57	write. A fresh call creates a fresh random email/password set. Partial failure
    58	does not claim rollback: some accounts/grants may exist; discard the disposable
    59	staging deployment or inspect it before retrying. Application data is created
    60	through ordinary authenticated mutations after provisioning.
    61	
    62	Credential records are returned to the operator, never logged by the helper.
    63	The tested guide writes them to an exclusively created 0600 file. They must

   255	## 9. Wave-19 identity retry and local production lifecycle
   256	
   257	Commission: Charlie's day-two addendum, wave-19 fixes #6/#7 (2026-10-19).
   258	This amends the SDK/proof and local release contracts; it grants no new auth
   259	or filesystem authority. SEC4 and QRY keep their existing scopes.
   260	
   261	Identity `guest`, `signup` and `login` share a portable request helper with
   262	proof `seedAccounts` (including `startServe({seedUsers})`). Only a delivered
   263	HTTP 429 containing a validated auth `E_RATE_LIMIT` refusal, not marked
   264	`retryable:false`, may retry. The server refuses these requests before account
   265	creation/authentication. Wait for nonnegative integer `retryAfterMs`, or a
   266	valid Retry-After header on older servers (otherwise one second). Preserve the
   267	same credentials and scope, without sending retry options on the wire. Up to
   268	four attempts fit inside the whole request deadline (`timeoutMs`, default
   269	180000); an AbortSignal cancels fetch and waiting. A wait that cannot fit
   270	returns the original refusal with its delay; setup instead throws
   271	E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, warning that partial accounts/grants may remain. Setup
   272	passes its remaining overall budget (default five minutes). There is no
   273	polling at a fixed short interval. Transport errors, malformed responses,
   274	other status/family/codes, permanent refusals, session rotations and role
   275	provisioning mutations never automatically replay. Account/role admission,
   276	peer/email/KDF limits and the staging-before-mint boundary stay unchanged.
   277	These deadlines rely on the fetch implementation honoring AbortSignal, as the
   278	standard fetch does. Custom fetch adapters must honor that contract too.
   279	
   280	Deploy and rollback may wait up to five seconds to acquire the actual owner
   281	flock before admission. Missing/unreachable address hints select bounded
   282	waiting; a responsive listener selects the existing authenticated control
   283	status path. If that read-only status fails while shutdown is underway, use
   284	only the remaining acquisition budget, then reread status under the acquired
   285	owner. Neither status nor an address/PID hint admits activation. A subsequent
   286	activation request or ambiguous reply is never replayed automatically. The
   287	exclusive flock, canonical inode/hardlink checks, private auxiliary files,
   288	revision CAS and immutable-source validation remain authoritative. Prune and
   289	other offline command semantics are unchanged. A surviving owner still
   290	refuses E_STORE_BUSY; no process is signalled based on a hint.
   291	
   292	`serve DIR --wait-stopped` exposes a five-second lock-release barrier for
   293	callers retaining their own process handle. It requires an existing database,
   294	opens only its existing hardened private owner sidecar, obtains an exclusive
   295	flock and validates the named sidecar/database inode. It does not open SQLite,
   296	create a deployment/sidecar, clear address metadata or signal a PID. No owner
   297	sidecar means no named ownership exclusion. The documented sidecar removal
   298	boundary of LLP 3000.019 §3.4 remains; this is a point-in-time barrier, not a
   299	reservation against a future owner. Other serve flags refuse before effects.
   300	
   301	Proof `startServe().stop()` first terminates/reaps the retained native child
   302	through the existing bounded TERM/KILL path, then awaits this barrier, including
   303	any watchdog-held descriptor during worker cleanup. Concurrent/repeated stops
   304	share the in-flight/successful operation. Failure rejects, clears the cached
   305	failure and allows a later barrier retry; it cannot falsely claim cleanup.
   306	No new PID lookup or automatic stop of another owner is introduced. The proof
   307	host stop allowance includes the native child and five-second store barrier.
   308	
   309	`data TABLE --json` returns `{rows, more, limit}` for empty and nonempty
   310	snapshots, replacing the bare array. `more` reports the existing one-extra-row
   311	probe in the same read transaction, including default 50-row truncation and
   312	`--limit 0`. Text JSON-lines and the stderr notice are preserved. This operator
   313	surface still bypasses application read rules and refuses private/ephemeral

   326	## 10. Wave-20 loop repairs (DX5)
   327	
   328	Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-20 fix list #4, #6, #7, #8;
   329	implementer Codex, 2026-10-21. This amendment is proposed until its two

   334	### Clock reports
   335	
   336	Amend LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4's proof helper return: `advance(duration)`
   337	returns `{now, fired, held}`. Each entry carries the schedule name, target,
   338	reason, boundary/window metadata and bounded run summary from the existing
   339	operator-only schedule report. `now()` still returns a number. The CLI and
   340	HTTP advance reply expose the same arrays, retaining `schedules` for existing
   341	operator consumers. Fired means a schedule was enqueued, not that its job
   342	succeeded; the run summary distinguishes parked or pending work. Every
   343	non-fired schedule appears in held with a reason, including an already
   344	processed boundary, a future saved boundary, initialization, a future window
   345	or an explicit hold. Saved boundaries survive restart: one fire per boundary,
   346	coalescing missed periods unless eachBoundary was explicitly requested.
   347	The helper and CLI print saved-boundary holds and their recovery action on
   348	stderr, including the equal-boundary case on a reused store. Advance never
   349	rewinds markers or replays a completed boundary. Reply limits account for the
   350	retained report plus its partition into fired/held. Staging's expiry notice
   351	describes expiry/upload recovery without development-door instructions.
   352	Ambiguous or failed advances are never retried; time may already have moved.
   353	Maintenance failures return an explicitly incomplete schedule report with the
   354	advanced time; the proof helper attaches this reply to its thrown error.
   355	
   356	### Source diagnostics without an existence oracle
   357	
   358	Extend LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2's N_LOOKUP_FILTERED advice to required reads
   359	and reads of written tables. A later write and an asserted `! else CODE` do
   360	not prove read authority. Existing key/flow proofs still suppress advice,
   361	including prior successful exact reads and deliberately public projections.
   362	One note names the source lookup, authored hiding rule, declaration and the
   363	null/custom-refusal consequence; duplicate N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN notes at that
   364	site are avoided (the more specific N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN takes precedence). This is missing-proof advice, not a claim every caller
   365	is refused. Program `exists` and rule-witness `exists` keep distinct semantics.
   366	
   367	For private tables with secondary unique keys, source advice explains that
   368	an unreadable conflicting row uses generic E_RULE (or an undisclosed write
   369	target miss), even when the unique declaration has `else CODE`. The named
   370	constraint applies only when the conflict can be disclosed. Do not return
   371	the declared code only on hidden conflicts: that would violate LLP 3000 §7
   372	and LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2. Public E_RULE repair text, if changed, is identical
   373	for ordinary rule rejection and hidden collision. No row, key, actual hiding
   374	clause or hidden-dependent meter enters the public refusal. Rewrites propose
   375	a minimal readable key projection or operator-mediated ownership/claim flow,
   376	never broader disclosure of private rows. Paired hidden/missing lookup tests assert equality of public diagnostics and
   377	logical meters. Hidden/ordinary write-refusal tests compare public refusals
   378	and receipts; write replies expose no meter.
   379	
   380	### Upgrade advice reaches the old CLI
   381	
   382	Extend §8's bounded scan with candidate `data ... --json` consumers in authored
   383	scripts, including argv-array and shell forms. List paths without printing
   384	source. State the one-line migration `JSON.parse(stdout).rows` for the former
   385	bare array, and preserve `more`/`limit`. This is a candidate scan, not an AST
   386	proof or an automatic rewrite; report scan limits.
   387	
   388	The installed wrapper runs project warnings before the first ordinary check
   389	for that installed version, independently of the runtime-history receipt.
   390	A warning receipt is written only after delivery to a terminal (or an empty
   391	scan). Piped/captured stderr cannot establish delivery: old quiet upgrades
   392	discard it, so a nonempty scan stays unacknowledged and the next ordinary
   393	check repeats the advice, including in CI. Baseline checks neither deliver
   394	nor acknowledge warnings; read/receipt failures do not fail compilation.
   395	Warnings always use stderr, preserving one-object JSON stdout and quiet-mode
   396	visibility. This reaches the usual published 0.4.33/0.4.35 upgrade path because
   397	their upgrade invokes the newly installed wrapper for check. A fresh-process
   398	resolution must select new bytes after package replacement. Direct upgrade
   399	keeps its existing pre-install warning behavior. Test both published old CLIs
   400	against the fresh packed package in an isolated local registry, including
   401	--quiet and --json --quiet and the deferred first check; do not claim
   402	an upgrade was tested by invoking only the new helper.
   403	
   404	### Frontend and starter custody
   405	
   406	Extend LLP 3000.013.002 §2 with `ReadState` in snapback4/react: a list read
   407	(or PageHook) renders loading, denied, empty, or authorized data through one
   408	component. It adds no subscription, cache or authority. It preserves partial
   409	and stale rows; empty means the returned list is empty, never proven absence.
   410	Loading and empty default to null; denied uses the supplied renderer or
   411	throws the existing QueryRefusal for an error boundary. Children receive the
   412	typed list and precise settled read metadata. Browser and React Native
   413	callers supply their own display elements.
   414	
   415	The Expo adapter owns `snapback4-expo/metro` (CommonJS withSnapback(config))
   416	and its wasm transformer. Resolve Expo's transformer relative to the consuming
   417	project/config, compatible with isolated package-manager installs. Preserve
   418	the caller's config and append the existing .snapback4 block and wasm support.
   419	New starter Metro config only obtains Expo's default and calls withSnapback.
   420	The adapter also owns the native smoke sign-in hook; new starters import it
   421	instead of carrying src/native-smoke.ts. Password and guest selection remain
   422	explicit; ordinary launches never sign in automatically. Adapt removes a recognized old helper only when the planned source no longer
   423	references it; custom references, modified helpers and unknown source symlinks
   424	retain application custody. Old generated Metro prose remains recognizable
   425	when adapting an untouched README. No native engine or simulator custody changes.
   426	
   427	Amend LLP 3000.011.003.000 §7.2: adapt replaces an untouched todo frontend
   428	proof with a runnable proof scaffold retaining frontend:proof/proof:web and
   429	Playwright. It starts the correct frontend and checks rendered content, then
   430	explicitly refuses to claim an app-specific write proof until the builder
   431	adds one. A public schema without identity or personas skips sign-in and still
   432	checks rendering before the missing-scenario refusal. A custom proof is never
   433	rewritten. Fresh non-todo starters get the
   434	same scaffold. Every Expo starter includes playwright-core, including custom
   435	schemas. Qualification runs changed guide/starter sources from the packed
   436	tarball, tests the expected scaffold refusal, and records frontend character
   437	reductions on copies of three wave-20 Expo lanes. No original lane is edited.

   449	## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)
   450	
   451	Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
   452	Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
   453	LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
   454	and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
   455	intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
   456	This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.
   457	
   458	### Session input and compatibility
   459	
   460	Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
   461	principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
   462	Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
   463	transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
   464	expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
   465	server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
   466	as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
   467	and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
   468	E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
   469	one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
   470	shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
   471	the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.
   472	
   473	### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries
   474	
   475	ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
   476	for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
   477	coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.
   478	
   479	For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
   480	lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
   481	fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
   482	in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
   483	the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
   484	become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
   485	refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
   486	families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
   487	Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
   488	deadlines/backoffs remain business time.
   489	
   490	Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
   491	response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
   492	and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
   493	through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
   494	new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
   495	such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
   496	including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
   497	time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
   498	bearer's matching request URL/header and monotonically increases its live
   499	expiry/cap before clock listeners run. Local/device clients await durable
   500	credential custody before publishing or persisting their business clock.
   501	Online clients keep a volatile clock; their existing session listeners may
   502	persist custody asynchronously. Authenticated restoration still validates
   503	expired metadata with the staging probe; no online durability barrier is implied.
   504	Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
   505	evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
   506	local/device clock publication are serialized: durable credential saves are awaited
   507	before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
   508	clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
   509	transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
   510	App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
   511	clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
   512	App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
   513	the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
   514	and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
   515	The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
   516	spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
   517	reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
   518	local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
   519	auth operation or remote revocation queue.
   520	Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
   521	before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
   522	An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
   523	completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
   524	Retention preserves a decoded body, not a stale authentication classification.
   525	An E_AUTH refusal remains scoped to the bearer revision actually dispatched:
   526	rotation supersedes prior and intermediate retiring-bearer revisions, including
   527	when the response was decoded before rotation or arrives after cancellation or
   528	a retryable refresh failure. Recheck that authority when consuming retained
   529	responses. A successor already dispatched during credential persistence remains
   530	current; its own refusal may sign it out. Sign-out alone does not supersede a
   531	same-bearer refusal, and sent outcomes and business refusals retain their ordinary
   532	invocation custody. Retryable refresh failure still permits a same-id retry under
   533	the current credential revision.
   534	Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
   535	clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
   536	own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
   537	an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
   538	staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
   539	without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
   540	reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
   541	check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
   542	absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
   543	and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
   544	ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
   545	credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
   546	business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
   547	all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
   548	credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
   549	This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
   550	ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.
   551	
   552	advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
   553	before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
   554	queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
   555	so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
   556	row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
   557	host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
   558	same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
   559	and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
   560	The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
   561	clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
   562	automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
   563	report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
   564	drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
   565	work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.
   566	
   567	A saved boundary is future-held only when it is strictly greater than the
   568	boundary of the requested effective schedule window. Equality means that the
   569	current window was already processed: report not-due, without consulting wall
   570	time. Repeated advances inside that window and zero-time drains succeed without
   571	allowHeld, including recovery of queued work after a failed drain completion.
   572	Never enqueue the processed window again.
   573	A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
   574	E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
   575	schedule, saved boundary, next unprocessed window and recovery duration to
   576	reach the saved boundary from the unchanged process clock, not from the rejected
   577	requested time. Relative recovery hints in accepted reports likewise use the
   578	actual process clock, including when a disclosure floor is ahead of it.
   579	A held report sets heldUntil to that saved boundary and
   580	nextBoundary to the next unprocessed boundary. Catching up to heldUntil
   581	reports not-due and never re-enqueues the processed window; reaching nextBoundary
   582	fires once. Fresh staging storage and continuing with the original offset are
   583	recovery choices; saved markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
   584	retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
   585	explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
   586	Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.
   587	
   588	### Upgrade advice and future formats
   589	
   590	Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
   591	version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
   592	for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
   593	The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
   594	older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
   595	that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
   596	Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
   597	guide changes remains available. No ancestor
   598	process inspection or script mutation is introduced.
   599	
   600	The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
   601	uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
   602	nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
   603	never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
   604	Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
   605	Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
   606	nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.
   607	
   608	### Starter and proof rendering
   609	
   610	Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and
   611	partial empty results retain distinct text, with existing freshness and
   612	pagination semantics unchanged. Rename the docs' local ReadState example to
   613	ReadNotice so it does not shadow the export. Password clients omit persona
   614	selection and explicit web witness/generated API imports. The proof driver installs the
   615	existing witness bridge before app creation; createApp calls an immutable Symbol observer only under explicit witness=web.
   616	This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication
   617	boundary. A witness URL alone installs no observer and exposes no App global.
   618	The driver installs its nonconfigurable/nonwritable observer before application
   619	scripts and locks/freezes the selected witness bridge; the first App remains
   620	selected for that page. Same-App explicit API registration can enrich it;
   621	a different explicit App refuses E_WITNESS_APP_SELECTION and requires a separate
   622	page. Later automatic Apps cannot silently redirect the proof. Application JS
   623	remains trusted to implement the application: same-origin code can forge its
   624	own test observer outside a driven page, just as it can read web session storage.
   625	The observer grants no new credentials or backend authority. Ordinary bundles
   626	carry only the creation dispatch, not the witness implementation. No-API
   627	registration captures only durable non-ephemeral mutation handles; direct
   628	witness mutate still requires generated API.
   629	
   630	Proof text locators match normalized entire descendant text, including composed
   631	React Native spans and wrapping labels. Choose smallest matching visible,
   632	non-editable elements; independent matches retain strict Playwright ambiguity.
   633	Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,
   634	with no Unicode normalization or input value matching. Exact strings are case-sensitive;
   635	explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
   636	String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
   637	fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
   638	Text ranges outside overflow clips do not contribute evidence to a visible
   639	ancestor. Layoutless wrappers may forward their visible descendants; a clipped
   640	suffix cannot manufacture a complete status label.

   689	## 12. Wave-24 loop repairs (DX7)
   690	
   691	Commission: Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22; implementer: Codex in sb4-b24-dx7.
   692	This amends §11, LLP 3000.036 §22.8 and the ordinary rule-helper exclusion.
   693	SEC8 owns security questionnaire/dispositions, presence intent, invariant test
   694	coverage and lifecycle advice; DX7 only reports their existing verdicts.
   695	Implementation and tests accompany this amendment; review readiness is distinct
   696	from author acceptance.
   697	
   698	### Durable staging time
   699	
   700	A staging store owns its cumulative offset and latest explicitly checkpointed
   701	business time. The additive typed metadata record also retains a pending
   702	maintenance pause. Production ignores this record and rejects clock controls;
   703	ordinary dev retains its process-local clock/reset contract. No release-format
   704	change or filesystem sidecar is needed. Store adapters use their existing
   705	metadata transaction and fencing, including Postgres.
   706	
   707	Startup resumes at the maximum of wall plus saved offset, checkpointed time,
   708	and the existing disclosure floor. Without a checkpoint, the latest retained
   709	commit/schedule boundary supplies the legacy recovery floor. Explicit startup
   710	offsets are absolute offsets from wall time, clamped to the resumed floor;
   711	restarting never adds the same offset twice or rewinds saved boundaries.
   712	The resulting effective offset is persisted at startup. Malformed checkpoints
   713	refuse startup rather than silently resetting. Downgrades to older binaries
   714	ignore this additive record and retain their historical process-local behavior.
   715	
   716	Each accepted staging advance checkpoints offset, time and paused=true in the
   717	same transaction that preserves eligible sessions and worker leases, before
   718	publishing the process clock or doing maintenance. A storage failure rolls back
   719	all those effects. A lost reply is still ambiguous and never automatically
   720	replayed. drain:false, a failed drain and an interrupted drain retain the pause
   721	across restart. A successful drain durably clears it only after due work has
   722	finished. If that final write fails, report an incomplete drain and retain the
   723	pause. A restart does not shift already-preserved credentials again. Clock
   724	status/advance reports say the offset belongs to this staging store. Coalescing,
   725	eachBoundary, current-window equality and explicit allowHeld keep §11 semantics.
   726	
   727	### Rendered and scrollable text
   728	
   729	Mounted text inside overflow:auto/scroll ancestors counts even when outside
   730	the scrollport: it can be reached by scrolling. The selector does not scroll
   731	or change application layout. Overflow:hidden/clip remains a real clip, with
   732	character geometry retaining only the displayed prefix; display:none,
   733	visibility:hidden/collapse, opacity:0 and content-visibility:hidden remain
   734	excluded, as do editable/input/script text and layoutless text. This does not
   735	claim occlusion detection or virtualized content that is not mounted. Existing
   736	normalization, smallest matching element and strict ambiguity remain unchanged.
   737	
   738	### Upgrade and gate presentation
   739	
   740	Upgrade snapshots count security notes alongside compiler notes and report
   741	pending review gates separately, with unavailable previous gate data stated
   742	honestly for old snapshots. The gate status reflects acknowledgments without
   743	writing them during reporting. A refuted invariant cannot be acknowledged:
   744	check explicitly reports that --ack-security was not applied, leaves review
   745	records untouched and explains that the policy/intent must be repaired.
   746	The JSON result carries the same explanation. Gate-only upgrade failures name
   747	check --ack-security <ID> --reason '<spec rationale>'; other failures retain
   748	schema/device remediation. An already published old CLI may still print its
   749	old E_UPGRADE line; the new check child must carry the actionable explanation.
   750	The release card records the 0.4.37 CLI's obsolete closed-door/startDev advice.
   751	The numeric-advance candidate scan requires an actual advance call in the same
   752	local expression/assignment as numeric consumption; unrelated operators or
   753	new Date/assert calls elsewhere in a file do not qualify.
   754	
   755	### Protected immutable payloads
   756	
   757	A column-read-protected payload may be immutable. On insert its supplied value
   758	is validated normally. On every update/existing-upsert, a supplied protected
   759	immutable field is ignored without comparing it with stored data, for every
   760	viewer, including its readers and the system. Its retained value and asset
   761	placement remain unchanged; absent-upsert still inserts. Compiler advice on an
   762	explicit patch names that behavior. Ordinary unprotected immutability retains
   763	its existing contract. Cap/unique/index/authority/derived dependencies on
   764	protected fields remain refused. This input-independent policy preserves
   765	LLP 3000.036 §22.8's noninterference oracle and needs no new device protocol:
   766	the same interpreter runs it on the server and device.
   767	
   768	### Audience helpers and hidden probes
   769	
   770	Expression-bodied helpers, or a block containing one return, may appear in
   771	table/column rules when expansion is exactly the existing rule grammar.
   772	Arguments are ordinary typed rule terms, substituted simultaneously without
   773	caller capture. Only parameters, viewer and rule constants may be free in the
   774	helper; a helper's focal dot cannot capture the caller's row. Nested helpers
   775	are bounded to eight levels and a bounded expanded-node budget; cycles,
   776	wrong arity/types, block effects/lets, arithmetic, clock and ordinary reads
   777	refuse with E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR and an actionable repair. No new runtime
   778	instruction, probe semantics, authority or resource allowance is introduced.

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#12-wave-24-loop-repairs-dx7 — staging owns time; legacy stores recover from retained evidence.
pub fn staging_clock(store: &snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore, requested: i64, wall: i64) -> Result<snapback4_core::metadata::StagingClock, RuntimeError> {
    use snapback4_core::metadata::{DevMetadata, StagingClock};
    let saved = store.dev_value(DevMetadata::StagingClock)?
        .map(|text| serde_json::from_str::<StagingClock>(&text)
            .map_err(|_| RuntimeError::Input("invalid persisted staging clock; refusing to reset staging time".into())))
        .transpose()?;
    if let Some(saved) = &saved { saved.validate()?; }
    let floor = store.time_audience_clock_value()?.map(|text| text.parse::<i64>()
        .map_err(|_| RuntimeError::Input("invalid staging disclosure clock".into()))).transpose()?.unwrap_or(0);
    let recovered = if let Some(saved) = &saved { wall.checked_add(saved.offset).unwrap_or(i64::MAX).max(saved.now) }
        else { wall.saturating_add(resume_offset(store, wall)?) };
    let now = wall.checked_add(requested).unwrap_or(i64::MAX).max(recovered).max(floor);
    let state = StagingClock { now, offset: now.saturating_sub(wall), paused: saved.is_some_and(|s| s.paused) };
    state.validate()?;
    Ok(state)
}

    /// Move held effect/action leases and their delegated viewer sessions
    /// together. Backoffs and ordinary sessions stay put; overdue stays overdue.
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — dev advances preserve worker lifetimes without making retries wait longer.
    pub fn advance_worker_leases(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.advance_worker_leases_at(milliseconds, crate::now_ms())
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.001.000#workers — keep live supervised bearers valid until their orderly clock-revision replacement.
    pub fn advance_worker_leases_at(&mut self, milliseconds: i64, before: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.advance_clock_leases_at(milliseconds, before, false)
    }

    /// Staging preserves credential lifetime by default; explicit expiry proofs
    /// pass false. Application deadlines and retry backoffs continue to advance.
    pub fn advance_staging_clock_at(&mut self, milliseconds: i64, before: i64, preserve_sessions: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.advance_clock_leases_at(milliseconds, before, preserve_sessions)
    }

    /// Persist business time before publishing it; preserve credentials only once.
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#12-wave-24-loop-repairs-dx7 — the checkpoint and lease/session shifts have one commit.
    pub fn checkpoint_staging_clock_at(&mut self, milliseconds: i64, before: i64, preserve_sessions: bool, clock: &crate::metadata::StagingClock) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        use crate::metadata::{DevMetadata, MetadataReader, MetadataWriter};
        clock.validate()?;
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        if tx.deployment_environment()?.as_deref() != Some("staging") {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input("clock checkpoint requires a staging store".into()));
        }
        if milliseconds < 0 { return Err(RuntimeError::Input("staging clock cannot move backwards".into())); }
        if milliseconds > 0 {
            if preserve_sessions { super::session_clock::preserve(&tx, milliseconds, before)?; }
            tx.shift_worker_leases(milliseconds, before)?;
        }
        tx.set_dev_value(DevMetadata::StagingClock, &serde_json::to_string(clock).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Input(e.to_string()))?)?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.009.001.000.000#k0a-implementation-note — staging extends the existing clock/worker transaction seam rather than adding a durable opener.
    fn advance_clock_leases_at(&mut self, milliseconds: i64, before: i64, preserve_sessions: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        if preserve_sessions { super::session_clock::preserve(&tx, milliseconds, before)?; }
        tx.shift_worker_leases(milliseconds, before)?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A claim whose lease ran out goes back to the queue: the worker died
    /// or stalled, and the attempt it took stays counted.
    pub fn requeue_expired_effects(&mut self, now: i64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
        let changed = expire(&tx, now)?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(changed)
    }

   699	
   700	A staging store owns its cumulative offset and latest explicitly checkpointed
   701	business time. The additive typed metadata record also retains a pending
   702	maintenance pause. Production ignores this record and rejects clock controls;
   703	ordinary dev retains its process-local clock/reset contract. No release-format
   704	change or filesystem sidecar is needed. Store adapters use their existing
   705	metadata transaction and fencing, including Postgres.
   706	
   707	Startup resumes at the maximum of wall plus saved offset, checkpointed time,
   708	and the existing disclosure floor. Without a checkpoint, the latest retained
   709	commit/schedule boundary supplies the legacy recovery floor. Explicit startup
   710	offsets are absolute offsets from wall time, clamped to the resumed floor;
   711	restarting never adds the same offset twice or rewinds saved boundaries.
   712	The resulting effective offset is persisted at startup. Malformed checkpoints
   713	refuse startup rather than silently resetting. Downgrades to older binaries
   714	ignore this additive record and retain their historical process-local behavior.
   715	
   716	Each accepted staging advance checkpoints offset, time and paused=true in the
   717	same transaction that preserves eligible sessions and worker leases, before
   718	publishing the process clock or doing maintenance. A storage failure rolls back
   719	all those effects. A lost reply is still ambiguous and never automatically
   720	replayed. drain:false, a failed drain and an interrupted drain retain the pause
   721	across restart. A successful drain durably clears it only after due work has
   722	finished. If that final write fails, report an incomplete drain and retain the
   723	pause. A restart does not shift already-preserved credentials again. Clock
   724	status/advance reports say the offset belongs to this staging store. Coalescing,
   725	eachBoundary, current-window equality and explicit allowHeld keep §11 semantics.
   726	
   727	### Rendered and scrollable text
   728	
   729	Mounted text inside overflow:auto/scroll ancestors counts even when outside

   732	character geometry retaining only the displayed prefix; display:none,
   733	visibility:hidden/collapse, opacity:0 and content-visibility:hidden remain
   734	excluded, as do editable/input/script text and layoutless text. This does not
   735	claim occlusion detection or virtualized content that is not mounted. Existing
   736	normalization, smallest matching element and strict ambiguity remain unchanged.
   737

   739	
   740	Upgrade snapshots count security notes alongside compiler notes and report

   751	The numeric-advance candidate scan requires an actual advance call in the same

   754	
   755	### Protected immutable payloads
   756	
   757	A column-read-protected payload may be immutable. On insert its supplied value
   758	is validated normally. On every update/existing-upsert, a supplied protected
   759	immutable field is ignored without comparing it with stored data, for every
   760	viewer, including its readers and the system. Its retained value and asset
   761	placement remain unchanged; absent-upsert still inserts. Compiler advice on an
   762	explicit patch names that behavior. Ordinary unprotected immutability retains
   763	its existing contract. Cap/unique/index/authority/derived dependencies on
   764	protected fields remain refused. This input-independent policy preserves
   765	LLP 3000.036 §22.8's noninterference oracle and needs no new device protocol:
   766	the same interpreter runs it on the server and device.

with `unknown` false, or a known refusal) compare the whole outcome record
except `seq` (and server-only `delivery`); every other read counts under a named
reason (`online-only-*`). Low ceilings reach the device only through `call`'s

Writes go through `admit`: a device refusal must equal the server's, a
predicted row must equal the committed one (less its `pending` marker), and
after `settle` plus a sync round the device must answer `observe` as the server
does. `run-devices` accepts `--seconds`. Known findings are retained under
`cases/found/device-*` with a `DIAGNOSIS.md`; `tests/devices.rs` replays them
and `tests/smoke.rs` pins the fixed-seed signature set.

The Lean oracle (`run-lean`, LLP 3000.035 §5.2): `snapback4_lang::emit::lean`
translates each generated program's surface tree (never the binder's IR) to
the model's case JSON; `quarry-oracle` (`lean/Oracle.lean`, one process per

default ceilings. Compared: kind, refusal code, data (tagged: an id is not a
text), `complete`, `next` presence, each side's own continuation, and a

outside the model's fragment are named unsupported reasons, never passes.
`lean::generate` adds Lean-only variants (per-effect rules, a hidden probe
target, nullable/id orders, residual filters) aimed at `lean/OPEN.md`. A

match the engine without a document. Findings live in

pins the open signature set. Lean-dependent tests skip loudly without the

Quarry scheduled testing: prepare a separate clean clone whose current branch
can fast-forward to `origin/main`. The runner fetches/fast-forwards it and starts
its own socket-only evaluation cluster with `fsync=off`,
`synchronous_commit=off`, `full_page_writes=off`, `shared_buffers=1GB`, and
`max_connections=200`. It builds the Lean model's `quarry-oracle` first
(`lake build` in `lean/`; a host without `lake` fails the run), then runs the
SQLite, store, device and Lean campaigns on the selected
seed window, replays shrunk findings twice, and files/appends open `issues/*.md`
tickets. Only ticket changes are committed/pushed, with three fetch/rebase
retries. State and reports live outside Git under `--state-dir`; seeds advance
only after completed work and successful owned-cluster cleanup. Dirty/diverged
trees, overlap, setup failures, partial reports and failed publication refuse.
A crash can retain the lock and cluster directory; inspect `lock/owner.json`
and the run report. Never stop a cluster by process name.

`--dry-run --cases 32` writes previews and a separate `next-seed.dry-run.json`,
never commits or pushes. Dry runs may explicitly supply `--external-postgres
'host=... user=... dbname=...'`; that cluster is neither started nor stopped by
the runner. Ambient connections do not override normal private-cluster ownership.
The installer remains an operator action; do not invoke it during development.

The Lean oracle on a scheduled host (one-time, per user, no sudo): install
elan with `curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leanprover/elan/master/elan-init.sh -sSf | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none`.

Mathlib), so the first scheduled run needs network. Check by hand with
`(cd lean && ./check.sh)` in the runner's clone. `run.json` records the pinned
toolchain and the oracle binary's digest.
